title.zh: 卷一百七十九 列傳第一百零四 李鄭二王賈舒
title.en: Volume 179 Biographies 104: Li, Zheng, Two Wangs, Jia, Shu
title.raw: 卷一百七十九 列傳第一百零四 李鄭二王賈舒 Volume 179 Biographies 104: Li, Zheng, Two Wangs, Jia, Shu

sentences.zh: 李鄭二王賈舒

translations.literal: Li, Zheng, two Wangs, Jia, and Shu
translations.idiomatic: Li, Zheng, the two Wangs, Jia, and Shu

sentences.zh: 李訓，字子垂，始名仲言，字子訓，故宰相揆族孫。

translations.literal: Li Xun, styled Zichui, was originally named Zhongyan with the style Zixun; he was a clansman of the former chief minister Li Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, whose courtesy name was Zichui, had originally been called Zhongyan and styled Zixun; he was a kinsman of the former chief minister Li Kui.

sentences.zh: 質狀魁梧，敏於辯論，多大言，自標置。

translations.literal: His physique was tall and imposing; he was quick in debate, prone to grand talk, and fond of self-promotion.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing, quick in debate, given to grandiloquence, and eager to set himself apart.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，補太學助教，辟河陽節度府。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant instructor at the Imperial University, and was recruited to the He-Yang military commission.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as an assistant instructor at the Imperial University, and entered the staff of the He-Yang military commission.

sentences.zh: 從父逢吉為宰相，以仲言陰險善謀事，厚昵之。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Li Fengji was chief minister; because Zhongyan was crafty and skilled at plotting affairs, Fengji treated him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: His father's younger cousin Li Fengji was chief minister and, seeing that Zhongyan was devious and skilled at intrigue, grew very close to him.

sentences.zh: 坐武昭獄，流象州。

translations.literal: He was implicated in the Wu-Zhao affair and banished to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Caught up in the Wu-Zhao case, he was exiled to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 文宗嗣位，更赦還，以母喪居東都。

translations.literal: When Wenzong succeeded to the throne, he was pardoned and returned, and lived in the Eastern Capital during his mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong took the throne, a general amnesty brought him back, and he remained in the Eastern Capital for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 鄭註佐昭義府，仲言慨然曰：「當世操權力者皆齪齪，吾聞註好士，有中助，可與共事。」

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu was assisting at the Zhaoyi headquarters. Zhongyan said with feeling, 'Those who wield power in our age are all petty; I hear Zhu esteems scholars and has Zhongzhu as patron—we can work with them.
translations.idiomatic: While Zheng Zhu was on the staff at Zhaoyi, Zhongyan said with feeling, 'The men who hold power today are all small-minded. I hear Zhu loves scholars and has Zhongzhu behind him—we could work with them.

sentences.zh: 因往見註，相得甚歡。

translations.literal: He went to see Zhu and they got on famously.
translations.idiomatic: He went to visit Zhu, and the two took to each other at once.

sentences.zh: 時逢吉方留守，怏怏不樂，思復用，知與註善，付金幣百萬，使西至京師厚結註。

translations.literal: Fengji was then left as regent and was discontent; wishing to be reappointed, knowing Zhu was on good terms with Zhongyan, he gave him a million in gold and silver to go west to the capital and bind Zhu closely.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was then serving as regent in Luoyang and was unhappy; eager to return to office and knowing Zhu was close to Zhongyan, he gave him a million in gold and silver to go west to the capital and win Zhu over completely.

sentences.zh: 註喜，介之謁王守澄。

translations.literal: Zhu was pleased and introduced him to Wang Shoucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was delighted and introduced him to Wang Shoucheng.

sentences.zh: 守澄善遇之，即以註術、仲言經義並薦於帝。

translations.literal: Shoucheng received him kindly and recommended both Zhu's arts and Zhongyan's classical learning to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng treated him well and recommended both Zhu's arts and Zhongyan's mastery of the classics to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 仲言持詭辯，激卬可聽，善鉤揣人主意，又以身儒者，海內望族，既見識擢，誌望不淺。

translations.literal: Zhongyan wielded sophistry in debate that excited and uplifted the listener; he was adept at probing people's intent. Because he was himself a Confucian from a great house of the realm, once he was recognized and promoted, his ambitions were not slight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan argued with a specious eloquence that stirred and lifted his hearers, and he was skilled at sounding out what others meant. He also presented himself as a Confucian from one of the empire's great families; once he was recognized and advanced, his ambitions were far from modest.

sentences.zh: 始，宋申錫謀誅守澄不克，死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Song Shenxi had plotted to kill Shoucheng but failed and died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Song Shenxi had plotted to kill Shoucheng but failed and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 宦尹益橫，帝愈憤恥。

translations.literal: The eunuch supervisors grew still more overbearing, and the emperor grew ever more angry and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch overseers grew still more domineering, and the emperor's anger and shame deepened.

sentences.zh: 而憲祖之弒，罪人未得，雖外假借，內不堪，欲夷絕其類，顧在位臣持祿取安，無仗節死難者。

translations.literal: Yet the assassins of Xianzong had not been brought to justice; though outwardly he had to feign accommodation, inwardly he could not bear it and wished to exterminate their kind—but the ministers in office clung to salary and ease, and none stood on principle to die for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the murderers of Emperor Xianzong had never been punished; though he had to feign accommodation outwardly, inwardly he could not endure it and wished to wipe out their whole class—yet the ministers in office clung to their salaries and comfort, and none would uphold principle and die for the cause.

sentences.zh: 註陰知帝指，屢建密計，引仲言葉力。

translations.literal: Zhu secretly knew the emperor's aim and repeatedly offered secret plans, drawing Zhongyan in to help.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu secretly understood what the emperor wanted and repeatedly offered secret plans, drawing Zhongyan in to share the effort.

sentences.zh: 帝外托講勸，又皆以守澄進，故與之謀則其黨不疑。

translations.literal: The emperor outwardly entrusted them with lecturing and counsel, yet all had been advanced through Shoucheng—so when he plotted with them his faction did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor outwardly relied on them for lectures and counsel, yet all had entered through Shoucheng—so when he plotted with them, Shoucheng's faction did not grow suspicious.

sentences.zh: 仲言尚缞粗，帝使衣戎服，號「王山人」，挾註出入禁中。

translations.literal: Zhongyan was still in coarse mourning dress; the emperor had him wear military garb, styled 'Master Wang the Recluse,' and he entered and left the Forbidden City with Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan was still in rough mourning garb; the emperor had him wear military dress, called him 'Master Wang the Recluse,' and let him enter and leave the inner palace with Zhu.

sentences.zh: 服除，起為四門助教，賜緋袍、銀魚，時太和八年也。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made Four Gates assistant instructor and granted a crimson robe and silver fish tag—it was the eighth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was appointed assistant instructor at the Four Gates, and was given a crimson robe and silver fish tally—it was the eighth year of the Taihe reign.

sentences.zh: 其十月，遷《周易》博士，兼翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was transferred to Doctor of the Book of Changes and also Hanlin attendant lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was promoted to Doctor of the Book of Changes and also made a Hanlin attendant lecturer.

sentences.zh: 入院，詔法曲弟子二十人侑宴，示優寵。

translations.literal: Entering the academy, the emperor ordered twenty students of the court music office to wait at banquets as a sign of special favor.
translations.idiomatic: On entering the Hanlin Academy, the emperor ordered twenty students of the court music office to attend his banquets as a mark of special favor.

sentences.zh: 於是給事中鄭肅、韓佽、諫議大夫李珝、郭承嘏、中書舍人高元裕、權璩等共劾仲言憸人，天下共知，不宜在左右。

translations.literal: Thereupon Supervising Secretariat Attendants Zheng Su and Han Qi, Remonstrating Officials Li Xu and Guo Chenggu, Secretariat Draftsmen Gao Yuanyi and Quan Zhu, and others jointly impeached Zhongyan as a flatterer known to all the realm, unfit to be at the emperor's side.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the supervising secretariat attendants Zheng Su and Han Qi, the remonstrating officials Li Xu and Guo Chenggu, the secretariat draftsmen Gao Yuanyi and Quan Zhu, and others jointly impeached Zhongyan as a sycophant known throughout the realm, unfit to remain at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not heed them.

sentences.zh: 仲言數進講，至閹寺，必感憤申重，以激帝心。

translations.literal: Zhongyan lectured repeatedly; whenever he came to eunuchs he would stir feeling and speak with grave earnestness to stir the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongyan lectured again and again; whenever his topic touched the eunuchs he would speak with moving earnestness and heavy emphasis to stir the emperor's heart.

sentences.zh: 帝見其言縱橫，謂果可任，遂不疑，而待遇莫與比，因改名訓。

translations.literal: The emperor, seeing his words far-ranging, thought he could indeed be entrusted, and no longer doubted him; his treatment was unmatched—and he was renamed Xun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, hearing how boldly he ranged in speech, decided he could indeed be trusted and no longer doubted him; no one received treatment like his—and he was given the name Xun.

sentences.zh: 帝猶慮宦人猜忌，乃疏《易》五義示群臣，有能異訓意者賞，欲天下知以師臣待訓。

translations.literal: The emperor still feared eunuch suspicion, so he circulated five interpretations of the Changes to the ministers, promising reward to any who differed from Xun's meaning, wishing all the realm to know he treated Xun as a teacher-minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor still feared the eunuchs' suspicion, so he circulated five expositions of the Changes to the ministers, promising a reward to anyone who disagreed with Xun's reading, wanting the whole realm to know he treated Xun as a teacher-minister.

sentences.zh: 明年秋七月，進翰林學士、兵部郎中，知制誥，居中倚重，實行宰相事。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following autumn he was advanced to Hanlin academician and bureau director of the Ministry of War, with draft edicts; he leaned on the center's weight and in fact performed the chief minister's duties.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the following autumn he was promoted to Hanlin academician and bureau director in the Ministry of War with authority to draft edicts; he leaned on the court's inner weight and in practice carried out the chief minister's work.

sentences.zh: 宦人陳弘誌時監襄陽軍，訓啟帝召還，至青泥驛，遣使者杖殺之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Chen Hongzhi was then supervising the Xiangyang army; Xun urged the emperor to recall him, and when he reached Qingni Post he sent an envoy who beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Chen Hongzhi was then supervising the Xiangyang army; Xun urged the emperor to recall him, and when he reached Qingni Post the emperor sent an envoy who beat him to death with staves.

sentences.zh: 復以計白罷守澄觀軍容使，賜鴆死。

translations.literal: By stratagem he had Shoucheng dismissed as army supervisor and given poisoned wine to die.
translations.idiomatic: By another stratagem he had Shoucheng removed as army supervisor and given poisoned wine to die.

sentences.zh: 又逐西川監軍楊承和、淮南韋元素、河東王踐言於嶺外，已行，皆賜死。

translations.literal: He also drove the western Sichuan army supervisor Yang Chenghe, Huai's Wei Suanyuan, and Hedong's Wang Jianyan to the outer marches; once they were sent off, all were ordered to die.
translations.idiomatic: He also drove the western Sichuan army supervisor Yang Chenghe, the Huainan supervisor Wei Suanyuan, and the Hedong supervisor Wang Jianyan to distant posts; once they had set out, all were ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 而崔潭峻前物故，詔剖棺鞭屍。

translations.literal: Cui Tanjun had died earlier; an edict ordered his coffin opened and his corpse flogged.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Tanjun had died earlier; an edict ordered his coffin opened and his corpse flogged.

sentences.zh: 元和逆黨幾盡。

translations.literal: The Yuanhe traitors were nearly all gone.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuanhe conspirators were nearly all eliminated.

sentences.zh: 訓本挾奇進，及大權在己，銳意去惡，故與帝言天下事，無不如所欲。

translations.literal: Zhu had originally entered by trading on novelty; once great power was in his hands he zealously removed evil—so whenever he spoke with the emperor of affairs under Heaven, nothing failed to go as wished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu had originally risen by trading on novelty; once great power was his, he zealously uprooted evil—so whenever he spoke with the emperor of affairs under Heaven, nothing failed to go as he wished.

sentences.zh: 與註相朋比，務報恩復仇，素忌李德裕、宗閔之寵，乃因楊虞卿獄，指為黨人，嘗所惡者，悉陷黨中，遷貶無闋日，班列幾空，中外震畏。

translations.literal: He and Zhu were allied as partners, bent on returning favors and taking revenge; he had long resented the favor shown Li Deyu and Zongmin, so through the Yang Yuqing case he denounced them as factionists; all he had hated were swept into the faction, and transfers and demotions knew no rest day—the court ranks were nearly empty, and within and without all trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhu were partners in alliance, bent on repaying favors and settling scores; he had long resented the favor shown Li Deyu and Niu Zongmin, so through the Yang Yuqing case he denounced them as factionists; everyone he had hated was swept into the faction, and transfers and demotions came day after day without pause—the court ranks were nearly empty, and inside and outside the palace all trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 帝為下詔開諭，群情稍安。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict of open reassurance, and popular feeling eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict of open reassurance, and public feeling eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 不逾月，以禮部侍郎同中書門下平章事，賜金紫服，仍詔三日一至翰林，以終《易》義。

translations.literal: Within a month he was made Vice Minister of Rites with concurrent appointment as Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, granted gold-purple dress; an edict still ordered him to come to Hanlin every three days to finish the meaning of the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he was made vice minister of rites with concurrent appointment as grand councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and granted gold-purple dress; an edict still required him to come to the Hanlin every three days to complete his exposition of the Changes.

sentences.zh: 訓起流人，一歲至宰相，謂遭時，其志可行。

translations.literal: Xun rose from banishment to chief minister in one year; he deemed the times favored him and his aims could be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had risen from exile to chief minister in a single year; he believed the times favored him and that his aims could be carried out.

sentences.zh: 欲先誅宦豎，乃復河、湟，攘夷狄，歸河朔諸鎮。

translations.literal: He wished first to execute the eunuch minions, then recover Hehuang, repel the barbarians, and return the Hebei garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He wished first to kill the eunuch minions, then recover the He and Huang regions, drive back the barbarians, and bring the Hebei garrisons back under the throne.

sentences.zh: 意果而謀淺，天子以為然。

translations.literal: His intent was bold but his schemes shallow—and the Son of Heaven thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: His aims were bold but his plans shallow—and the Son of Heaven believed him.

sentences.zh: 俄賜第勝業裏，賞賚旁午。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted a mansion in Shengye Lane, with rewards piled one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was granted a mansion in Shengye Lane, with rewards heaped one upon another.

sentences.zh: 每進見，它宰相備位，天子傾意，宦官衛兵皆慴憚迎拜。

translations.literal: Whenever he came to audience the other chief ministers were mere placeholders; the Son of Heaven bent his mind to him, and eunuch guards all cowered and bowed in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he came to audience the other chief ministers were mere placeholders; the Son of Heaven bent his full attention to him, and eunuch guards all cowered and bowed in welcome.

sentences.zh: 天下險怪士僥取富貴，皆憑以為資。

translations.literal: Adventurers throughout the realm who hoped for wealth and rank by crooked paths all used him as their ladder.
translations.idiomatic: Adventurers throughout the realm who hoped for wealth and rank by crooked paths all used him as their ladder.

sentences.zh: 訓時時進賢才偉望，以悅士心，人皆惑之。

translations.literal: Xun from time to time advanced men of talent and lofty reputation to please scholarly hearts, and people were all beguiled.
translations.idiomatic: Xun from time to time advanced men of talent and lofty reputation to please scholarly hearts, and people were all taken in.

sentences.zh: 嘗建言天下浮屠避傜賦，耗國衣食，請行業不如令者還為民。

translations.literal: He once proposed that Buddhist monks avoiding corvée and tax ate away the state's food and clothing, and asked that those whose profession fell short of the regulations be returned to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: He once proposed that Buddhist monks who evaded corvée and taxes consumed the state's food and clothing, and asked that those whose profession fell short of the regulations be returned to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 既執政，自白罷，因以市恩。

translations.literal: Once in power he himself proposed abolishing it, thus to buy favor.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power he himself proposed abolishing the measure, thereby to win favor.

sentences.zh: 始，註先顯，訓藉以進，及勢相埒，賴寵爭功，不兩立。

translations.literal: At first Zhu had risen first; Xun advanced by leaning on him—once their power was equal they relied on favor and fought for merit, and could not coexist.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhu had risen first and Xun advanced by leaning on him; once their power was equal they relied on imperial favor and fought for credit, and could not coexist.

sentences.zh: 然方事未集，乃出註使鎮鳳翔，外為助援，內實猜克，待逞，且殺之。

translations.literal: Yet when the affair was not yet concluded he sent Zhu out to command Fengxiang, outwardly as supporting aid, inwardly in fact suspicious and hostile—he waited for success and would then kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while the affair was still unfinished he sent Zhu out to command Fengxiang—outwardly as supporting aid, inwardly in fact suspicious and hostile—intending to kill him once success was achieved.

sentences.zh: 擢所厚善分總兵柄，於是王璠為太原節度使，郭行余為邠寧節度使，羅立言權京兆尹，韓約金吾將軍，李孝本權御史中丞。

translations.literal: He promoted his close favorites to divide military power: Wang Fan as Taiyuan military commissioner, Guo Xingyu as Binning commissioner, Luo Liyan acting as metropolitan magistrate, Han Yue as Gold Crow guard general, Li Xiaoben acting as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted his close favorites to divide military power among them: Wang Fan as Taiyuan military commissioner, Guo Xingyu as Binning commissioner, Luo Liyan as acting metropolitan magistrate, Han Yue as Gold Crow guard general, and Li Xiaoben as acting censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 陰許璠、行余多募士及金吾臺府卒，劫以為用。

translations.literal: He secretly promised Fan and Xingyu they would enlist many men and Gold Crow and tribunal office soldiers for use in the coup.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly promised Fan and Xingyu that they would recruit many men and soldiers from the Gold Crow guard and the tribunal offices for use in the coup.

sentences.zh: 十一月壬戌，帝御紫宸殿，約奏甘露降金吾左仗樹，群臣賀。

translations.literal: On renxu of the eleventh month the emperor held court in Zichen Hall; Yue reported that sweet dew had descended on the tree by the Gold Crow left guard, and the ministers congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day of the eleventh month the emperor held court in Zichen Hall; Han Yue reported that sweet dew had descended on the tree by the Gold Crow left guard, and the ministers offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 訓、元輿奏言：「甘露近在禁中，陛下宜親往以承天祉。」

translations.literal: Xun and Yuanheng memorialized, 'The sweet dew is close within the Forbidden City—the Your Majesty should go in person to receive Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and Wang Ya memorialized, 'The sweet dew is close within the inner palace—Your Majesty should go in person to receive Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: He assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 即輦如含元殿，詔宰相群臣往視。

translations.literal: The carriage went at once to Hanyuan Hall; he ordered chief ministers and court to go view it.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage went at once to Hanyuan Hall, and he ordered the chief ministers and the court to go view it.

sentences.zh: 還，訓奏言：「非甘露。」

translations.literal: On their return Xun memorialized, 'It is not sweet dew.
translations.idiomatic: On their return Xun memorialized, 'It is not sweet dew.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「豈約妄邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'Could Yue be lying?'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Could Yue be lying?'

sentences.zh: 顧中尉仇士良、魚誌弘等驗之，訓因欲閉止諸宦人，使無逸者。

translations.literal: He looked to the commandant-in-chief Qiu Shiliang, Yu Zhihong and others to examine it; Xun then wished to shut in all the eunuchs so none could escape.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the commandant-in-chief Qiu Shiliang, Yu Zhihong, and others to examine it; Xun then wished to shut in all the eunuchs so none could escape.

sentences.zh: 時璠、行餘皆辭赴鎮，兵列丹鳳門外，彀而待，訓傳呼曰：「兩鎮軍入受詔旨！」

translations.literal: Fan and Xingyu were then taking leave for their posts; troops lined up outside Danfeng Gate waiting in ambush. Xun called out, 'The two garrison armies enter to receive the edict!
translations.idiomatic: Fan and Xingyu were then taking leave for their posts; troops were drawn up outside Danfeng Gate lying in wait. Xun called out, 'The armies of the two circuits enter to receive the edict!

sentences.zh: 聞者趨入，邠寧軍不至，璠懼，弗能前，獨行余拜殿下。

translations.literal: Hearing this they rushed in; the Binning army did not arrive—Fan was afraid and could not advance; only Xingyu bowed below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this they rushed in; the Binning army did not arrive—Fan was afraid and could not advance; only Xingyu bowed below the hall.

sentences.zh: 宦人至仗所，約流汗不能舉首，士良等怪之曰：「將軍何為爾？」

translations.literal: When the eunuchs reached the guard station Yue sweated and could not raise his head; Shiliang and the rest said wonderingly, 'General, why are you like this?
translations.idiomatic: When the eunuchs reached the guard station Han Yue was sweating and could not raise his head; Shiliang and the rest said in surprise, 'General, why are you like this?

sentences.zh: 會風動廡幕，見執兵者，士良等驚，走出。

translations.literal: Then the wind moved the corridor screens and they saw armed men; Shiliang and the rest were startled and ran out.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wind stirred the corridor screens and they saw armed men; Shiliang and the rest were startled and ran out.

sentences.zh: 閽者將闔扉，為宦侍叱爭，不及閉。

translations.literal: The gatekeepers were about to shut the doors but eunuch attendants shouted in contention and they did not close in time.
translations.idiomatic: The gatekeepers were about to shut the doors, but eunuch attendants shouted in contention and they did not close in time.

sentences.zh: 訓急連呼金吾兵曰：「衛乘輿者，人賜錢百千！」

translations.literal: Xun urgently called again to the Gold Crow troops, 'Who guards the carriage—each man gets a hundred thousand in cash!
translations.idiomatic: Xun urgently called again to the Gold Crow troops, 'Whoever guards the carriage gets a hundred thousand in cash each!

sentences.zh: 於是有隨訓入者。

translations.literal: Thereupon some who had followed Xun entered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon some who had followed Xun in entered.

sentences.zh: 宦人曰：「急矣，上當還內！」

translations.literal: The eunuchs said, 'It is urgent—the sovereign must return inside!
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs cried, 'It is urgent—the sovereign must return inside!

sentences.zh: 即扶輦決罘罳下殿趨，訓攀輦曰：「陛下不可去！」

translations.literal: They at once supported the carriage, broke through the hanging screen below the hall and hurried off; Xun clung to the carriage saying, 'Your Majesty must not leave!'
translations.idiomatic: They at once supported the carriage, broke through the hanging screen below the hall, and hurried off; Xun clung to the carriage crying, 'Your Majesty must not leave!'

sentences.zh: 士良曰：「李訓反！」

translations.literal: Shiliang said, 'Li Xun has rebelled!'
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang cried, 'Li Xun has rebelled!'

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「訓不反。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, 'Xun has not rebelled.'
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, 'Xun has not rebelled.'

sentences.zh: 士良手搏訓而躓，訓壓之，將引刀靴中，救至，士良免。

translations.literal: Shiliang grappled with Xun hand to hand and stumbled; Xun pressed him down and was about to draw a knife from his boot when rescuers arrived and Shiliang escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Shiliang grappled with Xun hand to hand and stumbled; Xun pressed him down and was about to draw a knife from his boot when rescuers arrived and Shiliang escaped.

sentences.zh: 立言、孝本領眾四百東西來，上殿與金吾士縱擊，宦官死者數十人。

translations.literal: Liyan and Xiaoben led four hundred men east and west; they mounted the hall and with Gold Crow soldiers struck freely—several tens of eunuchs died.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Liyan and Li Xiaoben led four hundred men from east and west; they mounted the hall and with Gold Crow soldiers struck freely—several tens of eunuchs died.

sentences.zh: 訓持輦愈急，至宣政門，宦人郗誌榮揕訓，仆之，輦入東上閣，即閉，宮中呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Xun clung to the carriage ever more urgently; at Xuanzheng Gate the eunuch Xi Zhihong struck Xun down and he fell; the carriage entered the Upper Eastern Gate, which was shut at once, and within the palace they cried 'Long live!'
translations.idiomatic: Xun clung to the carriage ever more urgently; at Xuanzheng Gate the eunuch Xi Zhihong struck Xun down and he fell; the carriage entered the Upper Eastern Gate, which was shut at once, and within the palace they cried 'Long live!'

sentences.zh: 元輿雖知謀，不以告涯，曰：「上將開延英邪？」

translations.literal: Yuanheng knew the plot though he did not tell Ya, saying, 'Will the sovereign open Yanying?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya knew the plot though he did not tell others, saying, 'Will the sovereign open Yanying?

sentences.zh: 而群臣見宰相問故。

translations.literal: Yet the court group, seeing the chief minister, asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the court group, seeing the chief minister, asked what was happening.

sentences.zh: 會士良遣神策副使劉泰倫、陳君奕等率衛士五百挺兵出，所值輒殺。

translations.literal: Presently Shiliang sent the Shence deputy commissioners Liu Tailun, Chen Junyi and others leading five hundred guards with bared weapons; whom they met they killed.
translations.idiomatic: Presently Shiliang sent the Shence deputy commissioners Liu Tailun, Chen Junyi, and others leading five hundred guards with bared weapons; whom they met they killed.

sentences.zh: 涯等惶遽易服步出。

translations.literal: Ya and the rest in panic changed clothes and slipped out on foot.
translations.idiomatic: Ya and the rest in panic changed clothes and slipped out on foot.

sentences.zh: 殺諸司史六七百人，復分兵屯諸宮門，捕訓黨千餘人，斬四方館，流血成渠。

translations.literal: They killed six or seven hundred clerks of various offices, again divided troops to garrison the palace gates, captured more than a thousand of Xun's party and beheaded them at the Four Directions hostel—blood formed channels.
translations.idiomatic: They killed six or seven hundred clerks of various offices, again divided troops to garrison the palace gates, captured more than a thousand of Xun's party and beheaded them at the Four Directions hostel—blood formed channels in the ground.

sentences.zh: 宦豎知訓事連天子，相與怨嘖，帝懼，偽不語，故宦人得肆誌殺戮。

translations.literal: The eunuch minions knew Xun's affair touched the Son of Heaven and murmured together in resentment; the emperor was afraid and pretended not to speak, so the eunuchs could slaughter at will.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch minions knew Xun's affair touched the Son of Heaven and murmured together in resentment; the emperor was afraid and pretended not to speak, so the eunuchs could slaughter at will.

sentences.zh: 俄而元輿、涯皆為兵所執。

translations.literal: Before long Yuanheng and Ya were both seized by the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Ya and the rest were both seized by the troops.

sentences.zh: 涯實不知謀，士良榜笞急，乃自署反狀。

translations.literal: Ya had in truth not known the plot; under Shiliang's urgent flogging with the placard he signed his own confession of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Ya had in truth not known the plot; under Shiliang's urgent flogging with the placard he signed his own confession of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 詔出衛騎千餘，馳咸陽、奉天捕亡者，大索都城，分掩涯、訓等第，兵遂大掠，入黎埴、羅讓、渾鐬、胡證等家及賈耽廟，貲產一空。

translations.literal: An edict sent out over a thousand guard cavalry to gallop to Xianyang and Fengtian pursuing fugitives, searched the capital extensively, raided the mansions of Ya, Xun and others in turn—the troops then plundered on a great scale, entering the homes of Li Zhi, Luo Rang, Hun Hui, Hu Zheng and others and Jia Dan's temple until property was utterly empty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent out over a thousand guard cavalry to gallop to Xianyang and Fengtian pursuing fugitives, searched the capital extensively, and raided the mansions of Ya, Xun, and others in turn—the troops then plundered on a great scale, entering the homes of Li Zhi, Luo Rang, Hun Hui, Hu Zheng, and others and Jia Dan's temple until property was utterly empty.

sentences.zh: 兩省印、簿書輒持去，秘館圖籍，蕩然無余者。

translations.literal: The seals and registers of the two secretariats were carried off whenever met; the archive collections of the secret depot were swept bare, nothing remaining.
translations.idiomatic: The seals and registers of the two secretariats were carried off whenever met; the archive collections of the secret depot were swept bare, nothing remaining.

sentences.zh: 明日，召群臣朝，至建福門，從者不得入，光範門尚閉，列兵誰何，乃繇金吾右仗至宣政衙，兵皆露持。

translations.literal: Next day the emperor summoned the court to assembly at Jianfu Gate; followers could not enter; Guangfan Gate was still shut—troops lined up challenging who passed—and they went by way of the Gold Crow right guard to Xuanzheng yamen; the soldiers all bore weapons openly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor summoned the court to assembly at Jianfu Gate; followers could not enter; Guangfan Gate was still shut—troops lined up challenging who passed—and they went by way of the Gold Crow right guard to the Xuanzheng yamen; the soldiers all bore weapons openly.

sentences.zh: 是時無宰相、御史中丞，久之，閣門使馬元贄啟宣政扉傳詔，張仲方可京兆尹，而吏皆前死，群臣不能班。

translations.literal: At that time there was no chief minister or censor-in-chief. After a long while the gate attendant Ma Yuanyan opened the Xuanzheng doors and transmitted the edict: Zhang Zhongfang could be metropolitan magistrate—but the clerks had all died earlier and the court group could not take formation.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was no chief minister or censor-in-chief. After a long while the gate attendant Ma Yuanyan opened the Xuanzheng doors and transmitted the edict appointing Zhang Zhongfang metropolitan magistrate—but the clerks had all died earlier and the court group could not form ranks.

sentences.zh: 帝初未知涯等被系，猶遲其不朝，既而士良白涯與訓謀逆，將立鄭註。

translations.literal: At first the emperor did not know Ya and the rest were bound; he still delayed at their failure to attend court—then Shiliang reported that Ya and Xun had plotted rebellion and would install Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: At first the emperor did not know Ya and the rest had been seized; he still delayed at their failure to attend court—then Shiliang reported that Ya and Xun had plotted rebellion and would install Zheng Zhu.

sentences.zh: 遽召僕射令狐楚、鄭覃、兵部尚書王源中、吏部侍郎李虞仲等至，帝對悲憤，因付涯訊牒曰：「果涯書邪？」

translations.literal: He hastily summoned the Vice Directors Hu Chu, Zheng Qin, Minister of War Wang Yuanzhong, Vice Minister of Personnel Li Yuzhong and others; facing them the emperor spoke in grief and anger and handed them Ya's interrogation document saying, 'Is this truly Ya's writing?
translations.idiomatic: He hastily summoned the vice directors Hu Linghu Chu, Zheng Qin, Minister of War Wang Yuanzhong, Vice Minister of Personnel Li Yuzhong, and others; facing them the emperor spoke in grief and anger and handed them Ya's interrogation document, saying, 'Is this truly Ya's writing?

sentences.zh: 楚曰：「然！

translations.literal: Chu said, 'It is!
translations.idiomatic: Chu said, 'It is!

sentences.zh: 涯誠有謀，罪應死。」

translations.literal: Ya did indeed have a plot; the crime deserves death.'
translations.idiomatic: Ya did indeed have a plot; the crime deserves death.'

sentences.zh: 是日，京師兵剽劫未止，民乘亂，往往復私怨，相戕擊，人死甚眾。

translations.literal: That day capital troops' plunder had not ceased; the people, taking advantage of disorder, often settled private grudges and struck one another—very many died.
translations.idiomatic: That day the capital troops' plunder had not ceased; the people, taking advantage of the disorder, often settled private grudges and struck one another—very many died.

sentences.zh: 帝遣楊鎮、靳遂良等屯兵大衢，鼓而儆之，兵乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Yang Zhen, Jin Suiliang and others to station troops at the great thoroughfares and beat drums to warn them, and the soldiers then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Yang Zhen, Jin Suiliang, and others to station troops at the great thoroughfares and beat drums to warn them, and the soldiers then stopped.

sentences.zh: 帝逼宦官，於是下詔暴訓、涯等罪。

translations.literal: The emperor, pressed by the eunuchs, thereupon issued an edict exposing the crimes of Xun, Ya and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by the eunuchs, the emperor thereupon issued an edict exposing the crimes of Xun, Ya, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 孝本易綠誇，猶金帶，以帽障面，奔鄭註，至咸陽，追騎及之。

translations.literal: Xiaoben had changed out of his green-flowered finery but still wore the gold belt; he covered his face with a hat and fled toward Zheng Zhu—at Xianyang pursuing horsemen overtook him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoben had changed out of his green-flowered finery but still wore the gold belt; he covered his face with a hat and fled toward Zheng Zhu—at Xianyang pursuing horsemen overtook him.

sentences.zh: 餗匿民間，羸服乘驢自歸。

translations.literal: Su hid among the common people, wore emaciated garb, and came back on a donkey of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su hid among the people, dressed in ragged clothes, and returned on a donkey of his own accord.

sentences.zh: 璠聚河東兵環第自衛，弘誌使偏將攻之，呼曰：「王涯等得罪，起尚書為相。」

translations.literal: Fan gathered Hedong troops to ring his mansion in self-defense; Hongzhi sent a partial general to attack and called, 'Wang Ya and others have offended—the emperor has made you chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan gathered Hedong troops to ring his mansion in self-defense; Hongzhi sent a partial general to attack and called out, 'Wang Ya and the others have offended—the emperor has made you chief minister.

sentences.zh: 璠喜，啟關納之。

translations.literal: Fan was pleased, opened the gate and admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was pleased, opened the gate, and admitted them.

sentences.zh: 既行，知見紿，泣曰：「李訓累我。」

translations.literal: Once on the road he knew he had been deceived and wept, 'Li Xun has ruined me.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the road he knew he had been deceived and wept, 'Li Xun has ruined me.

sentences.zh: 俄行余、立言皆得。

translations.literal: Before long Xingyu and Liyan were also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xingyu and Liyan were also captured.

sentences.zh: 自涯十餘族並奴婢悉系左右軍。

translations.literal: From Ya onward more than ten clans together with male and female slaves were all bound in the Left and Right Armies.
translations.idiomatic: From Ya onward more than ten clans together with male and female slaves were all bound in the Left and Right Armies.

sentences.zh: 璠見涯，恚曰：「公何見引？」

translations.literal: Fan, seeing Ya, said in rage, 'Sir, why did you draw me in?
translations.idiomatic: Fan, seeing Ya, said in rage, 'Sir, why did you draw me in?

sentences.zh: 涯曰：「君昔漏宋丞相謀於守澄，今焉逃死？」

translations.literal: Ya said, 'You once leaked Chief Minister Song's plot to Shoucheng—how now do you escape death?'
translations.idiomatic: Ya said, 'You once leaked Chief Minister Song's plot to Shoucheng—how now do you escape death?'

sentences.zh: 訓既敗，被綠衣，詭言黜官，走終南山，依浮屠宗密。

translations.literal: After Xun's defeat he wore green robes, lied that he had been demoted, fled to Zhongnan Mountain and relied on the monk Zongmi.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun's defeat he wore green robes, lied that he had been demoted, fled to Zhongnan Mountain, and took refuge with the monk Zongmi.

sentences.zh: 宗密欲匿之，其徒不可，乃奔鳳翔，為盩厔將所執，械而東。

translations.literal: Zongmi wished to hide him, but his disciples would not allow it; he then fled to Fengxiang and was seized by a Zhouzhi garrison officer, shackled and sent east.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmi wished to hide him, but his disciples would not allow it; Xun then fled to Fengxiang, was seized by a Zhouzhi garrison officer, shackled, and sent east.

sentences.zh: 訓恐為宦人酷辱，祈監者曰：「得我者有賞，不如持首去。」

translations.literal: Xun feared cruel humiliation at the hands of the eunuchs and pleaded with his escort, saying, 'Whoever gets me alive will be rewarded—better take my head and go.
translations.idiomatic: Xun feared cruel humiliation by the eunuchs and pleaded with his escort: 'Whoever captures me alive will be rewarded—better take my head and go.

sentences.zh: 乃斬之，傳其首，餘黨悉禽。

translations.literal: Thereupon they beheaded him, sent his head ahead, and all the rest of the party were captured.
translations.idiomatic: They then beheaded him, sent his head ahead, and captured all his remaining followers.

sentences.zh: 後一日，兩神策兵將涯等赴郊廟，過兩市，皆腰斬梟首以徇。

translations.literal: The next day the two Shence armies took Ya and the others to the suburban temples; passing through the two markets, all were cut in two at the waist and their heads displayed as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the two Shence armies escorted Ya and the others to the suburban temples; passing through the two markets, all were cut in two at the waist and their heads displayed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 餗臨刑憤叱，獨元輿曰：「晁錯、張華尚不免，豈特吾屬哉？」

translations.literal: Su at execution raged and shouted; only Yuanyu said, 'Chao Cuo and Zhang Hua could not escape—how much less only our sort?
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su at execution raged and shouted; only Shu Yuanyu said, 'Chao Cuo and Zhang Hua could not escape unscathed—how much less only our sort?

sentences.zh: 約最後捕得，責以反狀，不服，斬之。

translations.literal: Yue was captured last; charged with the crime of rebellion, he would not confess and was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yue was captured last; charged with rebellion, he refused to confess and was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 殺訓弟仲褒、元臯。

translations.literal: They killed Xun's younger brothers Zhongbao and Yuantao.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Xun's younger brothers Zhongbao and Yuantao.

sentences.zh: 始，元臯以屬疏自解，得去，士良訊奴，言事前一昔宿訓第，遣人追斬之。

translations.literal: Earlier Yuantao, because his kinship was distant, had excused himself and been allowed to leave; Shiliang interrogated a slave who said that on the eve of the affair he had lodged at Xun's mansion—men were sent in pursuit and he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yuantao, pleading distant kinship, had been allowed to leave; Shiliang questioned a slave who said that on the eve of the affair he had stayed at Xun's mansion—pursuers were sent and he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 訓死，士良捕宗密，將殺之，怡然曰：「與訓遊久，浮屠法遇困則救，死固其分。」

translations.literal: After Xun's death Shiliang arrested Zongmi and was about to kill him; he said calmly, 'I traveled long with Xun; in the Buddhist law one saves those in distress—death is my portion.
translations.idiomatic: After Xun's death Shiliang arrested Zongmi and was about to kill him; Zongmi said calmly, 'I traveled long with Xun; in the Buddhist law one saves those in distress—death is my portion.

sentences.zh: 乃釋之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was released.
translations.idiomatic: He was then released.

sentences.zh: 是時暴屍旁午，有詔棄都外，男女孩嬰相雜廁。

translations.literal: At that time corpses lay piled everywhere; an edict ordered them cast outside the capital, boys and girls and infants mingled in heaps.
translations.idiomatic: At that time corpses lay piled everywhere; an edict ordered them cast outside the capital, boys and girls and infants mingled in heaps.

sentences.zh: 淹旬，許京兆府瘞斂，作二大冢，葬道左右。

translations.literal: After ten days the metropolitan government was permitted to bury them, making two great mounds and interring them on either side of the road.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days the metropolitan government was permitted to bury them, making two great mounds on either side of the road.

sentences.zh: 它日，帝頗思訓，數為李石、鄭覃稱其才。

translations.literal: Another day the emperor rather missed Xun and repeatedly praised his talent to Li Shi and Zheng Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Another day the emperor rather missed Xun and repeatedly praised his talent to Li Shi and Zheng Qin.

sentences.zh: 而宦豎益熾，帝末以制，居常忽忽不懌，每遊燕，雖倡樂雜沓，未嘗歡，顏慘不展，往往瞋目獨語，或裴回眺望，賦詩以見情，自是感疢，至棄天下雲。

translations.literal: Yet the eunuch minions grew still more rampant; the emperor could not control them at the end, and was habitually depressed and ill at ease. Whenever he went out in pleasure, though singers and musicians crowded about, he was never merry; his face was grim and unrelaxed, often glaring and talking to himself alone, or pacing and gazing afar, composing poems to show his mood—thereafter he fell ill and at last abandoned the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the eunuch minions grew still more rampant; the emperor could not control them in the end and was habitually depressed. Whenever he went out for pleasure, though singers and musicians crowded about, he was never merry; his face stayed grim, often glaring and talking to himself, or pacing and gazing afar, composing poems to show his mood—thereafter he fell ill and at last abandoned the realm.

sentences.zh: 鄭注，絳州翼城人。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu was a man of Yicheng in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu was from Yicheng in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 世微賤，以方伎遊江湖間。

translations.literal: His family was humble and low; he wandered the rivers and lakes practicing occult arts.
translations.idiomatic: His family was humble; he wandered the rivers and lakes practicing occult arts.

sentences.zh: 元和末，至襄陽，依節度使李愬。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuanhe reign he reached Xiangyang and attached himself to the military commissioner Li Su.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanhe reign he reached Xiangyang and attached himself to the military commissioner Li Su.

sentences.zh: 為愬煮黃金餌之，浸親遇，署衙推，從至徐州，稍參處軍政。

translations.literal: He boiled a golden elixir for Su to eat; gradually he won intimate favor, was appointed yamen aide, followed him to Xuzhou, and gradually took part in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared a golden elixir for Su to take; gradually he won intimate favor, was appointed yamen aide, followed him to Xuzhou, and gradually took part in military administration.

sentences.zh: 注多藝，詭譎陰狡，億探人廋隱，輒中所欲。

translations.literal: Zhu had many skills, was crafty and treacherous, guessed at people's hidden thoughts, and usually hit what they desired.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu had many skills, was crafty and treacherous, guessed at people's hidden thoughts, and usually hit what they desired.

sentences.zh: 為籌事，未嘗不用，挾邪市權，舉軍患之。

translations.literal: In planning affairs he was never not employed; he traded on wickedness to sell power, and the whole army resented him.
translations.idiomatic: In planning affairs he was always used; he traded on wickedness to sell power, and the whole army resented him.

sentences.zh: 監軍王守澄白愬，愬曰：「然彼奇士也，將軍試與語。」

translations.literal: The army supervisor Wang Shoucheng reported to Su; Su said, 'Yet he is an extraordinary man—General, try speaking with him.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor Wang Shoucheng reported to Su; Su said, 'Yet he is an extraordinary man—General, try speaking with him.

sentences.zh: 守澄始拒不納，既坐，機辯橫生，鉤得其意，守澄大驚，引至後堂，語終夕，恨相見晚。

translations.literal: Shoucheng at first refused to receive him; once seated, clever argument poured forth and he hooked Shoucheng's intent; Shoucheng was greatly startled, led him to the rear hall, and talked all night, regretting they had met so late.
translations.idiomatic: Shoucheng at first refused to receive him; once seated, clever argument poured forth and he hooked Shoucheng's intent; Shoucheng was greatly startled, led him to the rear hall, and talked all night, regretting they had met so late.

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「誠如公言。」

translations.literal: He apologized, saying, 'It is truly as you say.
translations.idiomatic: He apologized, saying, 'It is truly as you say.

sentences.zh: 即署巡官。

translations.literal: He was at once appointed patrol officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was at once appointed patrol officer.

sentences.zh: 守澄入總樞密，與俱至京師，厚加贍恤，日夜為守澄計議，因陰通賂遺。

translations.literal: When Shoucheng entered to head the Privy Council he brought Zhu with him to the capital, treated him with great generosity, and day and night made plans for Shoucheng, while secretly communicating bribes.
translations.idiomatic: When Shoucheng entered to head the Privy Council he brought Zhu with him to the capital, treated him with great generosity, and day and night made plans for Shoucheng, while secretly communicating bribes.

sentences.zh: 初士纖巧者附離，後要官貴人亦趨往。

translations.literal: At first clever minor scholars attached themselves; later important officials and nobles also hurried to him.
translations.idiomatic: At first clever minor scholars attached themselves; later important officials and nobles also hurried to him.

sentences.zh: 既陷宋申錫，搢紳側目。

translations.literal: Once he had trapped Song Shenxi, the gentry looked askance.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had trapped Song Shenxi, the gentry looked askance.

sentences.zh: 金吾將軍孟文亮鎮邠寧，取為司馬，不肯行，御史中丞宇文鼎劾奏，乃上道，過奉天輒還。

translations.literal: The Gold Crow general Meng Wenliang was military commissioner of Binning and took Zhu as his aide; Zhu refused to go. The censor-in-chief Yu Wendding impeached him, and only then did he take the road—but passing Fengtian he turned back.
translations.idiomatic: The Gold Crow general Meng Wenliang was military commissioner of Binning and took Zhu as his aide; Zhu refused to go. The censor-in-chief Yu Wendding impeached him, and only then did he take the road—but passing Fengtian he turned back.

sentences.zh: 御史復言注奸狀，請付有司治罪。

translations.literal: The censors again reported Zhu's wicked conduct and asked that he be handed to the authorities for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The censors again reported Zhu's wicked conduct and asked that he be handed to the authorities for punishment.

sentences.zh: 始，王涯用注力再輔政，又憚守澄，遏其奏。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Ya had used Zhu's strength to become chief minister twice, yet also feared Shoucheng and blocked the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Ya had used Zhu's strength to become chief minister twice, yet also feared Shoucheng and blocked the memorial.

sentences.zh: 更擢通王府司馬、右神策判官，士議讙駭。

translations.literal: He was further promoted to Prince of Tong's staff aide and right Shence adjutant; scholarly opinion was shocked and outraged.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Prince of Tong's staff aide and right Shence adjutant; scholarly opinion was shocked and outraged.

sentences.zh: 劉從諫惡其人，欲因斥去之，即表副昭義節度。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian hated the man and wished to have him driven out; he memorialized him as deputy to the Zhaoyi military commission.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian hated the man and wished to have him driven out; he memorialized him as deputy to the Zhaoyi military commission.

sentences.zh: 至府不旬月，文宗暴眩，守澄復薦注，即日召入，對浴堂門，賜賚至渥。

translations.literal: He had not been at headquarters a month when Wenzong suddenly fell ill; Shoucheng again recommended Zhu, and that same day he was summoned in, received audience at the Bath Hall gate, and gifts were lavished to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: He had not been at headquarters a month when Wenzong suddenly fell ill; Shoucheng again recommended Zhu, and that same day he was summoned in, received audience at the Bath Hall gate, and gifts were lavished to the utmost.

sentences.zh: 是夜，彗出東方，長三尺，芒耀怒急。

translations.literal: That night a comet appeared in the east, three feet long, its rays fierce and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: That night a comet appeared in the east, three feet long, its rays fierce and urgent.

sentences.zh: 俄進太僕卿，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Minister of the Imperial Stud and concurrent Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was advanced to Minister of the Imperial Stud and concurrent Censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 注資貪沓，既藉權寵，專鬻官射利，貲積鉅萬，不知止。

translations.literal: Zhu was greedy and grasping by nature; once he leaned on favor and power he monopolized the sale of offices and pursuit of profit, amassing tens of thousands in wealth without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was greedy and grasping by nature; once he leaned on favor and power he monopolized the sale of offices and pursuit of profit, amassing tens of thousands in wealth without cease.

sentences.zh: 起第善和裏，通永巷，飛廡復壁，聚京師輕薄子、方鎮將吏，以煽聲焰。

translations.literal: He built a mansion in Shanhe Lane connected to the Eternal Lane, with flying eaves and double walls, gathering the capital's frivolous youths and frontier generals to fan his renown.
translations.idiomatic: He built a mansion in Shanhe Lane connected to the Eternal Lane, with flying eaves and double walls, gathering the capital's frivolous youths and frontier generals to fan his renown.

sentences.zh: 間入神策，與守澄語必終日，或夜艾乃罷。

translations.literal: He would enter the Shence barracks from time to time; talks with Shoucheng always lasted all day, sometimes until midnight before ending.
translations.idiomatic: He would enter the Shence barracks from time to time; talks with Shoucheng always lasted all day, sometimes until midnight before ending.

sentences.zh: 險人躁夫有所幹謝，日走門。

translations.literal: Wicked and rash men with requests came daily to his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wicked and rash men with requests came daily to his gate.

sentences.zh: 李訓既附注進，於是兩人權震天下矣。

translations.literal: Once Li Xun had advanced by attaching to Zhu, the two men's power shook the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Xun had advanced by attaching to Zhu, the two men's power shook the realm.

sentences.zh: 尋擢工部尚書、翰林侍講學士，時訓已在禁中，日日議論帝前，相倡和，謀鉏翦中官，自謂功在晷刻，帝惑之。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Minister of Works and Hanlin attendant lecturer; Xun was already in the inner palace, discussing daily before the emperor, singing in unison, plotting to cut down the inner eunuchs, deeming success within the hour—the emperor was beguiled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Minister of Works and Hanlin attendant lecturer; Xun was already in the inner palace, discussing daily before the emperor, singing in unison, plotting to cut down the inner eunuchs, deeming success within the hour—the emperor was beguiled.

sentences.zh: 乘是進退士大夫，撓骫朝法，賢不肖淆亂，以為弛張當然。

translations.literal: Seizing this he advanced and dismissed scholar-officials, bent and twisted court law, good and bad mingled in confusion, deeming laxity and tightening natural.
translations.idiomatic: Seizing this he advanced and dismissed scholar-officials, bent and twisted court law, good and bad mingled in confusion, deeming laxity and tightening natural.

sentences.zh: 眾策其必亂。

translations.literal: The multitude predicted he would surely bring disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The multitude predicted he would surely bring disorder.

sentences.zh: 帝問富人術，以榷茶對。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the method of enriching the people; he answered with monopoly on tea.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked the method of enriching the people; he answered with monopoly on tea.

sentences.zh: 其法欲置茶官，籍民圃而給其直，工自擷暴，則利悉之官。

translations.literal: The method wished to set up tea officials, register the people's gardens and pay them price; the workers would pick and process themselves, and all profit would go entirely to the government.
translations.idiomatic: The method wished to set up tea officials, register the people's gardens and pay them price; the workers would pick and process themselves, and all profit would go entirely to the government.

sentences.zh: 帝始詔王涯為榷茶使。

translations.literal: The emperor first ordered Wang Ya as tea monopoly commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first ordered Wang Ya as tea monopoly commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又言秦、雍災，當興役厭之。

translations.literal: He also said Qin and Yong had disasters and labor projects should be raised to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: He also said Qin and Yong had disasters and labor projects should be raised to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗詠杜甫《曲江辭》，有「宮殿千門」語，意天寶時環江有觀榭宮室，聞註言，即詔兩神策治曲江、昆明，作紫雲樓、采霞亭，詔公卿得列舍堤上。

translations.literal: The emperor once chanted Du Fu's 'Qujiang' lines with 'palaces of a thousand gates'; thinking that in the Tianbao era pavilions and palace halls ringed the river, hearing Zhu's words he at once ordered the two Shence armies to work on Qujiang and Kunming, building the Purple Cloud Tower and the Cai Xia Pavilion, and ordered that chief ministers and court might set lodges on the embankment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once chanted Du Fu's 'Qujiang' lines with 'palaces of a thousand gates'; thinking that in the Tianbao era pavilions and palace halls ringed the river, hearing Zhu's words he at once ordered the two Shence armies to work on Qujiang and Kunming, building the Purple Cloud Tower and the Cai Xia Pavilion, and ordered that chief ministers and court might set lodges on the embankment.

sentences.zh: 注本姓魚，冒為鄭，故當時號「魚鄭」。

translations.literal: Zhu's original surname was Yu; he falsely took Zheng, so at the time he was called 'Fish Zheng.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's original surname was Yu; he falsely took Zheng, so at the time he was called 'Fish Zheng.'

sentences.zh: 及用事，人廋謂曰「水族」。

translations.literal: When he held power people secretly called him 'Aquatic Tribe.'
translations.idiomatic: When he held power people secretly called him 'Aquatic Tribe.'

sentences.zh: 貌寢陋，不能遠視，常衣粗裘，外示質素。

translations.literal: His appearance was homely and ugly; he could not see far and usually wore coarse furs, outwardly showing simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: His appearance was homely and ugly; he could not see far and usually wore coarse furs, outwardly showing simplicity.

sentences.zh: 始，李愬病痿，註治之有狀，守澄神其術，故中人皆昵愛。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Su was ill with paralysis; Zhu treated him with effect; Shoucheng marveled at his arts, so the inner eunuchs all grew fond of him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Su was ill with paralysis; Zhu treated him with effect; Shoucheng marveled at his arts, so the inner eunuchs all grew fond of him.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校尚書左僕射、鳳翔隴右節度使，詔月入奏事。

translations.literal: Before long he was made acting Left Vice Director and Fengxiang-Longyou military commissioner, with orders to enter court monthly to report.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting Left Vice Director and Fengxiang-Longyou military commissioner, with orders to enter court monthly to report.

sentences.zh: 請寮屬於訓，訓與舒元輿謀終殺注，慮其豪俊為助，更擇臺閣長厚者，以錢可復為副，李敬彜為司馬，盧簡能、蕭傑為判官，盧弘茂為掌書記。

translations.literal: He asked staff from Xun; Xun and Shu Yuanyu plotted finally to kill Zhu, fearing his bold followers as aid, and instead chose long-standing and generous men of the secretariat: Qian Kefu as deputy, Li Jingyi as aide, Lu Jianneng and Xiao Jie as adjutants, Lu Hongmao as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He asked staff from Xun; Xun and Shu Yuanyu plotted finally to kill Zhu, fearing his bold followers as aid, and instead chose long-standing and generous men of the secretariat: Qian Kefu as deputy, Li Jingyi as aide, Lu Jianneng and Xiao Jie as adjutants, Lu Hongmao as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 舊制，節度使受命，戎服詣兵部謁，後浸廢，注請復之，而王璠、郭行餘皆踵為常。

translations.literal: By old regulation when a military commissioner received appointment he wore military dress to visit the Ministry of War; later this was gradually abandoned; Zhu asked to restore it, and Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu all followed as custom.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation when a military commissioner received appointment he wore military dress to visit the Ministry of War; later this was gradually abandoned; Zhu asked to restore it, and Wang Fan and Guo Xingyu all followed as custom.

sentences.zh: 是日，度支、京兆等供帳。

translations.literal: That day the revenue commission, metropolitan government, and others supplied encampments.
translations.idiomatic: That day the revenue commission, metropolitan government, and others supplied encampments.

sentences.zh: 入辭，帝賜通天犀帶。

translations.literal: On farewell audience the emperor granted a belt of penetrating-heaven rhinoceros horn.
translations.idiomatic: On farewell audience the emperor granted a belt of penetrating-heaven rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 出都門，旗幹折，注惡之。

translations.literal: Outside the capital gate the flagpole broke; Zhu took it as ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the capital gate the flagpole broke; Zhu took it as ill omen.

sentences.zh: 先是，守澄死，以十一月葬滻水，注奏言：「守澄，國勞舊，願身護喪。」

translations.literal: Earlier Shoucheng had died and was to be buried at Chan water in the eleventh month; Zhu memorialized, 'Shoucheng was an old merit of the state—I wish to escort the funeral myself.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Shoucheng had died and was to be buried at Chan water in the eleventh month; Zhu memorialized, 'Shoucheng was an old merit of the state—I wish to escort the funeral myself.

sentences.zh: 因群宦者臨送，欲以鎮兵悉禽誅之。

translations.literal: Thus with the eunuch hosts attending the send-off he wished to use garrison troops to seize and execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: Thus with the eunuch hosts attending the send-off he wished to use garrison troops to seize and execute them all.

sentences.zh: 訓畏注專其功，乃先五日舉事。

translations.literal: Xun feared Zhu would monopolize the credit and so moved the affair five days earlier.
translations.idiomatic: Xun feared Zhu would monopolize the credit and so moved the affair five days earlier.

sentences.zh: 注率五百騎至，扶風令韓遼知其謀，奔武功。

translations.literal: Zhu led five hundred horsemen there; the Fufeng magistrate Han Liao knew the plot and fled to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu led five hundred horsemen there; the Fufeng magistrate Han Liao knew the plot and fled to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 注聞訓敗，乃還。

translations.literal: Zhu heard Xun had failed and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu heard Xun had failed and then returned.

sentences.zh: 其屬魏弘節勸注殺監軍張仲清及大將賈克中等十餘人，注驚撓不暇聽。

translations.literal: His follower Wei Hongjie urged Zhu to kill the army supervisor Zhang Zhongqing and the great generals Jia Kezhong and more than ten others; Zhu was too flustered to listen.
translations.idiomatic: His follower Wei Hongjie urged Zhu to kill the army supervisor Zhang Zhongqing and the great generals Jia Kezhong and more than ten others; Zhu was too flustered to listen.

sentences.zh: 仲清與前少尹陸暢用其將李叔和策，訪注計事，斬其首，兵皆潰去。

translations.literal: Zhongqing and the former junior metropolitan magistrate Lu Chang used their general Li Shuhe's stratagem, visited Zhu on the pretext of planning affairs, and beheaded him; the troops all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing and the former junior metropolitan magistrate Lu Chang used their general Li Shuhe's stratagem, visited Zhu on the pretext of planning affairs, and beheaded him; the troops all scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 注妻兄魏逢尤佻險，贊注為奸，數顧賕，為率更令、鳳翔少尹。

translations.literal: Zhu's wife's brother Wei Feng was especially frivolous and dangerous, aiding Zhu in wickedness, repeatedly looking to bribes; he was made director of the imperial workshops and junior prefect of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's wife's brother Wei Feng was especially frivolous and dangerous, aiding Zhu in wickedness, repeatedly looking to bribes; he was made director of the imperial workshops and junior prefect of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 遣逢至京師與訓約，被誅。

translations.literal: He sent Feng to the capital to arrange with Xun and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Feng to the capital to arrange with Xun and was executed.

sentences.zh: 可復等及親卒千餘人皆族矣。

translations.literal: Kefu and the rest together with close soldiers more than a thousand were all clan-extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Kefu and the rest together with close soldiers more than a thousand were all clan-extinguished.

sentences.zh: 擢仲清內常侍，遼咸陽令，叔和檢校太子賓客，賜錢千萬，暢鳳翔行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Zhongqing was promoted to inner attendant; Liao made Xianyang magistrate; Shuhe made acting Crown Prince guest; a gift of ten million in cash; Chang made Fengxiang campaigning staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqing was promoted to inner attendant; Liao made Xianyang magistrate; Shuhe made acting Crown Prince guest; a gift of ten million in cash; Chang made Fengxiang campaigning staff aide.

sentences.zh: 梟注首光宅坊，三日瘞之，群臣皆賀，乃夷其家。

translations.literal: Zhu's head was displayed at Guangzhai Ward; after three days it was buried; the court group all congratulated, and then his family was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu's head was displayed at Guangzhai Ward; after three days it was buried; the court group all congratulated, and then his family was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 初，未獲注，京師戒嚴，涇原、鄜坊節度使王茂元、蕭弘皆勒兵備非常。

translations.literal: Earlier, before Zhu was taken, the capital was under strict guard; the Jingyuan and Zhenfang military commissioners Wang Maoyuan and Xiao Hong both mobilized troops against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Zhu was taken, the capital was under strict guard; the Jingyuan and Zhenfang military commissioners Wang Maoyuan and Xiao Hong both mobilized troops against the unexpected.

sentences.zh: 及是人相慶。

translations.literal: When it was done people congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When it was done people congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 籍其貲，得絹百萬匹，它物稱是。

translations.literal: His property was registered: a million bolts of silk were obtained, and other goods in proportion.
translations.idiomatic: His property was registered: a million bolts of silk were obtained, and other goods in proportion.

sentences.zh: 注敗前，菌生所服帶上，褚中藥化為蠅數萬飛去。

translations.literal: Before Zhu's defeat fungus grew on the belt he wore, and medicine in his bag turned into tens of thousands of flies that flew away.
translations.idiomatic: Before Zhu's defeat fungus grew on the belt he wore, and medicine in his bag turned into tens of thousands of flies that flew away.

sentences.zh: 可復，徽子也，為禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Kefu was Hui's son and served as bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Kefu was Hui's son and served as bureau director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 簡能者，簡辭弟，駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: Jianneng was Jian's younger brother, an aide in the Ministry of Transport.
translations.idiomatic: Jianneng was Jian's younger brother, an aide in the Ministry of Transport.

sentences.zh: 傑者，俛弟也，主客員外郎。

translations.literal: Jie was Fu's younger brother, an aide in the Ministry of Receptions.
translations.idiomatic: Jie was Fu's younger brother, an aide in the Ministry of Receptions.

sentences.zh: 弘茂，右拾遺。

translations.literal: Hongmao was a right remonstrating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Hongmao was a right remonstrating censor.

sentences.zh: 可復將死，女年十四，為祈免，女曰：「殺我父，何面目以生！」

translations.literal: When Kefu was about to die his daughter, fourteen years old, prayed for his release; the girl said, 'You kill my father—how can I face living!
translations.idiomatic: When Kefu was about to die his daughter, fourteen years old, prayed for his release; the girl said, 'You kill my father—how can I face living!

sentences.zh: 抱可復求死，亦斬之。

translations.literal: She embraced Kefu and begged to die and was also beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: She embraced Kefu and begged to die and was also beheaded.

sentences.zh: 弘茂妻蕭，臨刑詬曰：「我太后妹，奴輩可來殺！」

translations.literal: Hongmao's wife Xiao at execution cursed, 'I am the empress dowager's sister—you slaves dare come kill!
translations.idiomatic: Hongmao's wife Xiao at execution cursed, 'I am the empress dowager's sister—you slaves dare come kill!

sentences.zh: 兵皆斂手，乃免。

translations.literal: The soldiers all stayed their hands and she was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers all stayed their hands and she was spared.

sentences.zh: 弘節勇而多謀，始在鄜坊趙儋節度府，為注所辟。

translations.literal: Hongjie was brave and full of schemes; he had first been in the Zhenfang Zhao Dan military commission and was recruited by Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Hongjie was brave and full of schemes; he had first been in the Zhenfang Zhao Dan military commission and was recruited by Zhu.

sentences.zh: 敬彜為路隋所辟，隋卒，客江淮，以未赴免，因擢兵部員外郎，終衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingyi was recruited by Lu Sui; when Sui died he sojourned on the Jiang-Huai, was excused for not having gone, and was then promoted to aide in the Ministry of War, ending as Quzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi was recruited by Lu Sui; when Sui died he sojourned on the Jiang-Huai, was excused for not having gone, and was then promoted to aide in the Ministry of War, ending as Quzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 王涯，字廣津，其先本太原人，魏廣陽侯冏之裔。

translations.literal: Wang Ya, styled Guangjin, his ancestors were originally from Taiyuan, descendants of the Wei Guangyang Marquis Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya, styled Guangjin, his ancestors were originally from Taiyuan, descendants of the Wei Guangyang Marquis Tong.

sentences.zh: 祖祚，武后時諫罷萬象神宮知名；

translations.literal: His grandfather Zuo was famed in Empress Wu's time for remonstrating to abolish the Palace of Myriad Images;
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zuo was famed in Empress Wu's time for remonstrating to abolish the Palace of Myriad Images;

sentences.zh: 開元時，以大理司直馳傳決獄，所至仁平。

translations.literal: in the Kaiyuan era, as assistant director in the Court of Judicial Review he traveled post-haste to decide cases, and wherever he went was humane and fair.
translations.idiomatic: in the Kaiyuan era, as assistant director in the Court of Judicial Review he traveled post-haste to decide cases, and wherever he went was humane and fair.

sentences.zh: 父晃，歷左補闕、溫州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Huang served as left remonstrator and Wenzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huang served as left remonstrator and Wenzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 涯博學，工屬文。

translations.literal: Ya was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was broadly learned and skilled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 往見梁肅，肅異其才，薦於陸贄。

translations.literal: He went to see Liang Su; Su marveled at his talent and recommended him to Lu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: He went to see Liang Su; Su marveled at his talent and recommended him to Lu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 擢進士，又舉宏辭，再調藍田尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and also passed the macro-elocution examination, and was twice transferred as Lantian county aide.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and also passed the macro-elocution examination, and was twice transferred as Lantian county aide.

sentences.zh: 久之，以左拾遺為翰林學士，進起居舍人。

translations.literal: After a long while he was made Hanlin academician from left remonstrator and advanced to attendant on the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was made Hanlin academician from left remonstrator and advanced to attendant on the emperor's movements.

sentences.zh: 元和初，會其甥皇甫湜以賢良方正對策異等，忤宰相，涯坐不避嫌，罷學士，再貶虢州司馬，徙為袁州刺史。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanhe era his nephew Huangfu Shi passed the extraordinary erudite policy examination with highest rank, offending the chief minister; Ya was punished for not avoiding suspicion, removed as academician, twice demoted to Guozhou aide, and transferred to Yuanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yuanhe era his nephew Huangfu Shi passed the extraordinary erudite policy examination with highest rank, offending the chief minister; Ya was punished for not avoiding suspicion, removed as academician, twice demoted to Guozhou aide, and transferred to Yuanzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 憲宗思之，以兵部員外郎召，知制誥，再為翰林學士，累遷工部侍郎，封清源縣男。

translations.literal: Xianzong thought of him, summoned him as aide in the Ministry of War with draft edicts, again made Hanlin academician, and repeatedly promoted him to Vice Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Baron of Qingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong thought of him, summoned him as aide in the Ministry of War with draft edicts, again made Hanlin academician, and repeatedly promoted him to Vice Minister of Works, enfeoffed as Baron of Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 涯文有雅思，永貞、元和間，訓誥溫麗，多所稿定。

translations.literal: Ya's writing had elegant purpose; in the Yongzhen and Yuanhe eras his edicts and orders were warm and beautiful, and many were drafted by him.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's writing had elegant purpose; in the Yongzhen and Yuanhe eras his edicts and orders were warm and beautiful, and many were drafted by him.

sentences.zh: 帝以其孤進自樹立，數訪逮，以私居遠，或召不時至，詔假光宅裏官第，諸學士莫敢望。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he had risen alone and established himself, frequently sought him out; because his private residence was far, sometimes when summoned he did not arrive in time—an edict lent him an official mansion in Guangzhai Lane that no other academician dared match.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because he had risen alone and established himself, frequently sought him out; because his private residence was far, sometimes when summoned he did not arrive in time—an edict lent him an official mansion in Guangzhai Lane that no other academician dared match.

sentences.zh: 俄拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，坐循默不稱職罷。

translations.literal: Before long he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, but was dismissed for routine silence and not fitting the post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat with concurrent appointment as Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, but was dismissed for routine silence and not fitting the post.

sentences.zh: 再遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was again transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，出為劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: When Muzong succeeded he went out as Eastern Sichuan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong succeeded he went out as Eastern Sichuan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃寇邊，西北騷然，又略雅州，涯調兵拒之。

translations.literal: At that time the Tibetans raided the frontier and the northwest was disturbed; they also seized Yazhou; Ya mobilized troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Tibetans raided the frontier and the northwest was disturbed; they also seized Yazhou; Ya mobilized troops to resist them.

sentences.zh: 上言：「蜀有兩道直搗賊腹，一繇龍川清川以抵松州，一繇綿州威蕃柵抵棲雞城，皆虜險要地。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Shu has two routes that pierce straight into the enemy's belly—one via Longchuan and Qingchuan to reach Songzhou, one via Mianzhou and Weifan Stockade to reach Qiji Castle—all critical places held by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "Shu offers two routes straight into the enemy heartland—one through Longchuan and Qingchuan to Songzhou, another through Mianzhou and Weifan Stockade to Qiji Castle—each a strategic stronghold held by the foe.

sentences.zh: 臣願不愛金帛，使信臣持節與北虜約曰：『能發兵深入者，殺某人，取某地，受某賞。』

translations.literal: Your servant wishes to spare no gold and silk, and to send a trusted envoy bearing credentials to treaty with the northern barbarians, saying: 'Whoever can dispatch troops deep into [enemy territory]—kill so-and-so, take such-and-such place, receive such-and-such reward.
translations.idiomatic: I am willing to spend gold and silk freely and send a trusted envoy with imperial credentials to treat with the northern tribes, promising: 'Whoever can march deep into enemy country—kill this man, seize that place, and receive this reward.

sentences.zh: 開懷以示之，所以要約諄熟異它日者，則匈奴之銳可出，西戎之力衰矣。」

translations.literal: Opening his heart to display this, making the covenant familiar and detailed unlike other days, then the Xiongnu's sharp forces can emerge, and the Western Rong's strength will decline.
translations.idiomatic: Lay the terms open before them and bind the agreement in careful detail unlike any past arrangement, and the Xiongnu's best troops can be brought out while the Western Rong's power wanes.

sentences.zh: 帝不報。

translations.literal: The emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made no response.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年，入為御史大夫，遷戶部尚書、鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Changqing, he entered [the capital] as Censor-in-Chief and was transferred to Minister of Revenue and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Changqing he returned to court as Censor-in-Chief, then became Minister of Revenue and Salt and Iron Transport Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寶歷時，復出領山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: During the Baoli era, he again went out to serve as military commissioner of the Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoli reign he was again sent out as military commissioner of the Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 文宗嗣位，召拜太常卿，以吏部尚書代王播，復總鹽鐵，政益刻急。

translations.literal: When Wenzong succeeded, he was summoned and appointed Minister of Imperial Sacrifices; as Minister of Personnel he replaced Wang Bo, again oversaw salt and iron, and his governance grew ever more harsh and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, Wang Ya was summoned as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, then replaced Wang Bo as Minister of Personnel while resuming control of salt and iron; his policies grew increasingly severe.

sentences.zh: 歲中，進尚書右僕射、代郡公。

translations.literal: Within the year he was advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before the year was out he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Duke of Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 而御史中丞宇文鼎以涯兼使職，恥為之屈，奏：「僕射視事日，四品以上官不宜獨拜。」

translations.literal: But Censor-in-Chief Yu Wen Ding, seeing that Ya also held a commissioner post, was ashamed to bow before him and memorialized: "On the day the Vice Director assumes office, officials of fourth rank and above ought not to bow alone.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding, resenting that Ya also held a commissioner's portfolio, refused to submit and memorialized: "On the day the Vice Director takes up his duties, officials of fourth rank and above should not bow to him alone.

sentences.zh: 涯怒，即建言：「與其廢禮，不如審官，請避位以存舊典。」

translations.literal: Ya grew angry and immediately proposed: "Rather than abolish ritual, it is better to examine the office—I request to vacate the post to preserve the old precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Ya was furious and countered: "Rather than discard proper ceremony, let us examine the office itself—I ask to step aside so the old precedent may stand."

sentences.zh: 帝難之，詔尚書省雜議。

translations.literal: The emperor found it difficult [to decide] and ordered the Department of State Affairs to deliberate collectively.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not settle the matter and ordered the Department of State Affairs to debate it jointly.

sentences.zh: 工部侍郎李固言謂：「《禮》：君於士不答拜，非其臣則答，不臣人之臣也；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Works Li Guyan said: "The Rites states: a lord does not return bows to common officers; to one who is not his subject he returns a bow—not one subject of another's subject;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Works Li Guyan argued: "The Rites teach that a ruler does not return a bow to a common officer, but does return one to someone who is not his subject—meaning, not the subject of another man's subject;

sentences.zh: 大夫於其臣，雖賤必答拜，避正君也；

translations.literal: a grand officer to his subject, even if lowly, must return a bow—to defer to the rightful lord;
translations.idiomatic: a grand officer to his own subordinate, however humble, must return the bow, deferring to the true sovereign;

sentences.zh: 大夫於獻不親，君有賜不面拜，為君之答己也。

translations.literal: a grand officer at tribute does not approach personally; when the lord has a gift one does not bow facing the lord—for the lord's return bow to oneself.
translations.idiomatic: a grand officer does not personally receive tribute; when the ruler bestows a gift one does not bow facing him—for the ruler has already returned the bow to oneself.

sentences.zh: 古者列國君猶與大夫答拜，所以尊事天子，別嫌明微也。

translations.literal: In antiquity even feudal lords still returned bows to grand officers—thereby to honor service to the Son of Heaven and clarify distinctions and subtle meanings.
translations.idiomatic: In ancient times even feudal lords exchanged bows with grand officers, thereby honoring their service to the Son of Heaven and marking distinctions with precision.

sentences.zh: 議者謂『僕射代尚書令，禮當重。

translations.literal: Debaters said 'The Vice Director substitutes for the Director—the rites ought to be weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued that 'the Vice Director stands in for the Director of the Department, and the ceremony ought to carry full weight.

sentences.zh: 凡百司州縣皆有副貳，缺則攝總，至著定之禮，則不可越，僕射由是也』。

translations.literal: Every bureau in prefecture and county has a deputy; when the chief is absent the deputy acts in charge—but once fixed ritual is established it cannot be overstepped; the Vice Director is thus.'
translations.idiomatic: Every office in the provinces and counties has a deputy who assumes charge when the chief is absent, yet once ritual is formally fixed it may not be overridden—the Vice Director is such a case.'

sentences.zh: 按令，凡文武三品拜一品，四品拜二品。

translations.literal: According to regulations, in general civil and military officials of third rank bow to first rank, fourth rank to second rank.
translations.idiomatic: Under statute, civil and military officials of third rank bow to those of first rank, and those of fourth rank bow to those of second rank.

sentences.zh: 《開元禮》，京兆河南牧、州刺史、縣令上日，丞以下答拜。

translations.literal: The Kaoyuan Rites: on the inaugural day of the Metropolitan and Henan governors, prefects, and county magistrates, aides and below return bows.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaoyuan Rites prescribe that on the inaugural day of the Metropolitan and Henan governors, prefects, and county magistrates, their deputies and subordinates return the bow.

sentences.zh: 此禮令相戾，不可獨據。」

translations.literal: These rites and regulations conflict and cannot be relied on alone."
