translations.idiomatic: These ritual codes and administrative regulations contradict one another and cannot be cited in isolation."

sentences.zh: 又言：「受冊官始上，無不答拜者，而僕射亦受冊，禮不得異。

translations.literal: He also said: "Officials receiving seals on first taking office—none fail to return bows; the Vice Director also receives seals, and the rites cannot differ.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Every official invested with a seal on first assuming office receives returned bows, and the Vice Director receives a seal as well—the ceremony cannot be an exception.

sentences.zh: 雖相承為故事，然人情難安者，安得弗改？

translations.literal: Though long followed as precedent, yet where human feeling finds it hard to accept, how can it not be changed?
translations.idiomatic: It may have become custom, but where custom unsettles men's hearts, how can we refuse to amend it?

sentences.zh: 請如禮便。」

translations.literal: Please follow the rites as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Let the rites be followed as they prescribe.

sentences.zh: 帝不能決，涯竟用舊儀。

translations.literal: The emperor could not decide; Ya ultimately used the old ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not reach a decision, and Ya kept the old practice after all.

sentences.zh: 自李師道平，三道十二州皆有銅鐵官，歲取冶賦百萬，觀察使擅有之，不入公上。

translations.literal: From the pacification of Li Shidao, the three circuits' twelve prefectures all had copper and iron bureaus, annually collecting smelting levies of a million; observation commissioners kept them for themselves and did not turn them in to the public treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Shidao's defeat, the twelve prefectures of three circuits each maintained copper and iron offices that collected a million in smelting taxes every year; the observation commissioners kept the revenue for themselves instead of forwarding it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 涯始建白：「如建中元年九月戊辰詔書，收隸天子鹽鐵。」

translations.literal: Ya first memorialized: "As in the edict of the ninth month, wuchen day, of the first year of Jianzhong, collect and subordinate [these revenues] to the Son of Heaven's salt and iron [administration].
translations.idiomatic: Ya first proposed: "Follow the edict of the wuchen day of the ninth month in the first year of Jianzhong—bring salt and iron revenues back under imperial control.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 久之，以本官同中書門下平章事，合度支、鹽鐵為一使，兼領之。

translations.literal: After a long while, with his existing office he became concurrent Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery; revenue and salt and iron were merged into one commission, which he also headed.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made Grand Councillor while retaining his existing post, and the revenue and salt-and-iron commissions were combined into one office under his direction.

sentences.zh: 乃奏罷京畿榷酒錢以悅眾。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to abolish the capital-region wine monopoly levy to please the people.
translations.idiomatic: He then proposed abolishing the capital's wine monopoly tax to win public favor.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校司空，兼門下侍郎。

translations.literal: Before long he was made acting Inspector of Works and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was appointed acting Inspector of Works and Vice Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 罷度支，真拜司空。

translations.literal: Revenue [commission] was abolished; he was formally appointed Inspector of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The revenue commission was dissolved, and he received formal appointment as Inspector of Works.

sentences.zh: 始變茶法，益其稅以濟用度，下益困，而鄭註亦議榷茶，天子命涯為使，心知不可，不敢爭。

translations.literal: He first changed the tea law, increasing its tax to meet expenditures; the common people grew still more distressed. Zheng Zhu also proposed a tea monopoly; the Son of Heaven ordered Ya as commissioner—Ya knew in his heart it would not do, yet did not dare contend.
translations.idiomatic: He revised the tea law, raising its tax to cover state expenses, and the people suffered all the more. Zheng Zhu likewise urged a tea monopoly; the emperor named Ya commissioner. Ya knew it was unwise but dared not object.

sentences.zh: 李訓敗，乃及禍。

translations.literal: When Li Xun was defeated, [Ya] then met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xun fell, Wang Ya was swept into ruin.

sentences.zh: 初，民怨茶禁苛急，涯就誅，皆群詬詈，抵以瓦礫。

translations.literal: Earlier the people resented the tea prohibition as harsh and urgent; when Ya was put to death they all cursed him in crowds and pelted him with tiles and stones.
translations.idiomatic: The people had long resented the harsh tea monopoly; when Ya was executed they mobbed his corpse, cursing him and pelting it with rubble.

sentences.zh: 涯質狀頎省，長上短下，動舉詳華。

translations.literal: Ya's physique was tall and spare, long above and short below; in movement and bearing he was refined and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya was tall and lean, with long torso and short legs, and carried himself with polished grace.

sentences.zh: 性嗇儉，不畜妓妾，惡卜祝及它方伎。

translations.literal: By nature he was frugal and sparing, kept no singing girls or concubines, and detested diviners and other occult arts.
translations.idiomatic: He was austere by nature, kept no concubines or entertainers, and despised fortune-tellers and every sort of occult craft.

sentences.zh: 別墅有佳木流泉，居常書史自怡，使客賀若夷鼓琴娛賓。

translations.literal: His villa had fine trees and flowing springs; he usually amused himself with books and histories, and had his guest He Ruoyi play the zither to entertain visitors.
translations.idiomatic: His country estate boasted fine timber and running water; he passed his days among books and histories, and had his guest He Ruoyi play the zither for company.

sentences.zh: 文宗惡俗侈靡，詔涯懲革。

translations.literal: Wenzong detested vulgar extravagance and ordered Ya to punish and reform it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong loathed vulgar luxury and charged Ya with curbing it.

sentences.zh: 涯條上其制，凡衣服室宇，使略如古，貴戚皆不便，謗訕囂然，議遂格。

translations.literal: Ya itemized regulations on it; for clothing and dwellings he made them roughly like antiquity—the noble clans all found it inconvenient, slander and clamor arose, and the proposal was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Ya drafted detailed regulations, prescribing clothing and dwellings roughly in ancient style; the great families all chafed at the restrictions, outcry mounted, and the plan was shelved.

sentences.zh: 然涯年過七十，嗜權固位，偷合訓等，不能絜去就，以至覆宗。

translations.literal: Yet Ya, past seventy, clung to power and held his post, truckling with Xun and the rest, unable to keep his conduct clean in advance or retreat—until he destroyed his clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet past seventy Wang Ya still hungered for power, clinging to office and colluding with Li Xun and his circle rather than keeping his hands clean—until his whole house was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 是時，十一族貲貨悉為兵掠，而涯居永寧裏，乃楊憑故第，財貯鉅萬，取之彌日不盡。

translations.literal: At that time the property of all eleven clans was thoroughly plundered by soldiers; Ya lived in Yongning Lane—it had been Yang Ping's former mansion—and stored wealth in the tens of thousands; taking it filled days without exhausting it.
translations.idiomatic: By then soldiers had looted the estates of all eleven clans. Ya's residence in Yongning Lane—once Yang Ping's mansion—held wealth counted in the tens of thousands; plundering it took days and still did not finish.

sentences.zh: 家書多與秘府侔，前世名書畫，嘗以厚貨鉤致，或私以官，鑿垣納之，重復秘固，若不可窺者。

translations.literal: His household books nearly matched the secret archive; famous calligraphy and painting of past ages he often hooked in with heavy payment, or privately used office to [obtain them], chiseled walls to bring them in, repeatedly sealed and secured them as if they could not be seen.
translations.idiomatic: His library nearly rivaled the imperial collection; he often paid lavish sums for celebrated paintings and calligraphy of earlier ages, sometimes trading official favor for them, breaking through walls to smuggle pieces inside and sealing them away as though invisible.

sentences.zh: 至是為人破垣剔取奩軸金玉，而棄其書畫於道。

translations.literal: At this time men broke the walls, picked out caskets, scroll rods, gold and jade, and cast the books and paintings aside on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Now looters smashed his walls, stripped out jewel caskets and scroll mounts, and left his books and paintings strewn in the streets.

sentences.zh: 籍田宅入於官。

translations.literal: Fields and dwellings were registered and entered into government [ownership].
translations.idiomatic: His fields and houses were inventoried and confiscated by the state.

sentences.zh: 子孟堅為工部郎中、集賢殿學士，仲翔太常博士，季琰校書郎，皆死。

translations.literal: His son Mengjian was aide in the Ministry of Works and Hanlin academician; Zhongxiang was Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; Jiyan was collator— all died.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Mengjian, an aide in the Ministry of Works and Hanlin academician; Zhongxiang, an Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; and Jiyan, a collator—all perished.

sentences.zh: 仲翔始匿侍御史裴鐇家，鐇執以赴軍，仲翔曰：「業不見容，當自求生，奈何反相噬邪？」

translations.literal: Zhongxiang at first hid in the home of Assistant Censor Pei Zhen; Zhen seized him and delivered him to the army. Zhongxiang said: "My line finds no room— I ought to seek life for myself; why turn and devour one another?
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiang first hid with Assistant Censor Pei Zhen, but Zhen seized him and handed him over to the troops. Zhongxiang cried: "Our house is already doomed—I should be trying to save myself; why turn on me like this?

sentences.zh: 聞者哀之。

translations.literal: Those who heard it pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 後令狐楚見帝，從容言：「向與臣並列者，既族滅矣，而露胔不藏，深可悼痛。」

translations.literal: Later Linghu Chu saw the emperor and said at ease: "Those who lately stood with your servant have already been exterminated to the clan, yet their exposed corpses lie unburied— deeply to be mourned and grieved.
translations.idiomatic: Later Linghu Chu saw the emperor and said gently: "Those who recently served beside me have been wiped out to the last kin, yet their bodies lie exposed and unburied—a sight too painful to bear.

sentences.zh: 帝惻然，詔京兆尹薛元賞葬涯等十一人，各賜襲衣。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved; he ordered Capital Intendant Xue Yuanshang to bury Ya and the other eleven men, each granted burial garments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with sorrow and ordered Capital Intendant Xue Yuanshang to bury Wang Ya and the other ten men, granting each a burial robe.

sentences.zh: 仇士良使盜竊發其冢，投骨渭水。

translations.literal: Qiu Shiliang had robbers secretly open their tombs and cast the bones into the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Shiliang sent thieves to break open the graves and throw the bones into the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 涯女為竇紃妻，以痼病免，家人紿告涯當貶，忽夢涯自提首告曰：「族滅矣，惟若存，歲時無忘我。」

translations.literal: Ya's daughter was wife to Dou Xuan; because of chronic illness she was spared. The family deceived her, saying Ya was to be demoted; suddenly she dreamed Ya carrying his own head and telling her: "The clan is destroyed; only you remain— do not forget me at the seasonal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya's daughter, wife of Dou Xuan, was spared because of chronic illness. Her family lied that Ya was merely being demoted; then she dreamed Ya holding his severed head and saying: "The clan is gone and only you survive—do not forget me at the seasonal offerings.

sentences.zh: 女驚號墮地，乃以實告。

translations.literal: The daughter cried out in shock and fell to the ground; then they told her the truth.
translations.idiomatic: She screamed and collapsed; only then was she told what had really happened.

sentences.zh: 涯從弟沐，客江南，困窮來京師謁涯，二歲乃得見，許以祿仕，難作，亦死。

translations.literal: Ya's younger clansman Mu, sojourning in the south, came destitute to the capital to visit Ya; after two years he finally gained an audience. [Ya] promised him an official salary and post; when the calamity arose, he too died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ya's cousin Mu, living as a guest in the south, came penniless to the capital to see him; only after two years did he obtain an audience, and Ya promised him office and salary. When disaster struck, he died as well.

sentences.zh: 昭宗天復初，大赦，明涯、訓之冤，追復爵位，官其後裔。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianfu in Zhaozong's reign, a great amnesty clarified the injustice done to Ya and Xun, restored their titles, and gave office to their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianfu era under Emperor Zhaozong, a general amnesty cleared the wrong done to Wang Ya and Li Xun, restored their ranks, and appointed their descendants to office.

sentences.zh: 賈餗，字子美，河南人。

translations.literal: Jia Su, styled Zimei, was a man of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su, courtesy name Zimei, came from Henan.

sentences.zh: 少孤，客江淮間。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he sojourned between the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his parents young and wandered the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 從父全觀察浙東，餗往依之，全尤器異，收恤良厚。

translations.literal: His father's younger cousin Quan was observation commissioner of Zhedong; Su went to rely on him—Quan especially valued and distinguished him, receiving and caring for him with great kindness.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Quan served as observation commissioner of Zhedong; Su went to live under his patronage. Quan admired him greatly and treated him with exceptional generosity.

sentences.zh: 舉進士高第，聲稱籍甚。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi with highest rank; his reputation was very great.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination at the top of his class and won wide renown.

sentences.zh: 又策賢良方正異等，授渭南尉、集賢校理。

translations.literal: He also passed the extraordinary erudite upright and exceptional policy examination and was appointed aide of Weinan and collator in the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He also passed the extraordinary erudite upright and exceptional policy examination and was appointed aide of Weinan county and Hanlin collator.

sentences.zh: 擢累考功員外郎，知制誥。

translations.literal: Promoted repeatedly to aide in the Ministry of Personnel and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to aide in the Ministry of Personnel and imperial edict drafter.

sentences.zh: 餗美文辭，開敏有斷，然褊急，氣陵輩行。

translations.literal: Su was fine in literary composition, open and quick with judgment, yet narrow and impatient, his spirit overbearing toward peers.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su wrote elegantly, was alert and decisive, yet was touchy and overbearing toward colleagues.

sentences.zh: 李渤為諫議大夫，惡其人，為宰相言之，而李逢吉、竇易直愛餗才，得不斥。

translations.literal: Li Bo was remonstrating censor and detested the man; he spoke of him to the chief minister—yet Li Fengji and Dou Yizhi loved Su's talent, so he was not dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating Censor Li Bo loathed him and complained to the chief minister, but Li Fengji and Dou Yizhi prized Jia Su's talent, so he kept his place.

sentences.zh: 穆宗崩，告哀江、浙，道拜常州刺史。

translations.literal: When Muzong died, [Su] announced mourning in Jiang and Zhe; en route he was appointed prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong died, Jia Su was sent to announce mourning in Jiangsu and Zhejiang and, while on the road, was appointed prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 舊制，兩省官出使，得朱衣吏前導。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when officials of the two secretariats went on mission, vermilion-robed clerks went before as guides.
translations.idiomatic: Under longstanding custom, envoys from the two secretariats were preceded by clerks in vermilion robes.

sentences.zh: 餗赴州，猶用之，觀察使李德裕敕吏還，怏怏為憾。

translations.literal: Su went to his prefecture and still used them; Observation Commissioner Li Deyu ordered the clerks back—[Su] nursed resentment as a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su still employed them on his way to Changzhou; Observation Commissioner Li Deyu sent the clerks back, leaving Su simmering with resentment.

sentences.zh: 入為太常少卿，復知制誥，歷禮部侍郎，凡三典貢舉，得士七十五人，多名卿宰相。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, again drafted edicts, served successively as Vice Minister of Rites, and three times presided over the tribute examinations, obtaining seventy-five men—many became famous ministers and chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Vice Minister of Imperial Sacrifices, resumed drafting edicts, served as Vice Minister of Rites, and presided over the civil examinations three times, selecting seventy-five men, many of whom became leading ministers.

sentences.zh: 再遷京兆尹、兼御史大夫、姑臧縣男。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Capital Intendant, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, Baron of Guzang county.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Capital Intendant, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and enfeoffed as Baron of Guzang county.

sentences.zh: 太和九年上巳，詔百官會曲江。

translations.literal: On the shangsi day of the ninth year of Taihe, an edict ordered all officials to assemble at Qujiang.
translations.idiomatic: On the shangsi festival in the ninth year of Taihe, the emperor ordered the whole bureaucracy to gather at Qujiang.

sentences.zh: 故事，尹自門步入，揖御史。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Intendant entered on foot from the gate and bowed to the censors.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the Capital Intendant entered on foot through the gate and exchanged bows with the censors.

sentences.zh: 餗自矜大，不徹扇蓋，騎而入。

translations.literal: Su, self-important and grand, did not remove his parasol canopy and rode in.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su, swollen with pride, did not fold his parasol canopy and rode straight in.

sentences.zh: 御史楊儉、蘇特固爭，餗曰：「黃面兒敢爾！」

translations.literal: Censors Yang Jian and Su Te firmly contended; Su said: "You yellow-faced boys dare such a thing!"
translations.idiomatic: Censors Yang Jian and Su Te protested fiercely. Jia Su snapped: "You yellow-faced whelps dare behave like this!"

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「公為御史，能嘿嘿耶？」

translations.literal: Jian said: "You serve as censor—can you keep silent, hmm?"
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian retorted: "And you, a censor—can you really say nothing?"

sentences.zh: 大夫溫造以聞。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Wen Zao reported the affair to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 坐奪俸，不勝恚，求出為浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: For this he was fined salary; unable to bear the rage, he requested transfer out as observation commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He was fined a month's salary; unable to swallow the humiliation, he asked to leave the capital as observation commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 未行，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and concurrent Grand Councillor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 俄為集賢殿大學士、監修國史。

translations.literal: Before long he was Grand Academician of the Hanlin Academy and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he became Grand Academician of the Hanlin Academy and chief editor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 既得位，會李宗閔得罪，而指儉、特為黨，斥去之。

translations.literal: Once he had attained position, when Li Zongmin was punished he identified Jian and Te as faction members and drove them out.
translations.idiomatic: Once in power, after Li Zongmin's fall he marked Yang Jian and Su Te as faction men and had them removed.

sentences.zh: 少與沈傳師善，傳師前死，嘗夢云：「君可休矣！」

translations.literal: In youth he was close to Shen Chuanshi; before Chuanshi died he once dreamed [Chuanshi] saying: "You may rest now!
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was close to Shen Chuanshi; before Chuanshi died Jia Su once dreamed him saying: "You can stop now!

sentences.zh: 餗寤而祭諸寢，復夢曰：「事已爾，叵奈何！」

translations.literal: Su awoke and made offerings in the bedchamber; he dreamed again [Chuanshi] saying: "The matter is already done—what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su woke, made offerings in his bedchamber, and dreamed again: "It is already settled—what can you do?"

sentences.zh: 劉蕡以賢良方正對策，指中人為禍亂根本，而餗與馮宿、龐嚴為考官，畏避不敢聞，竟罹其禍。

translations.literal: Liu Zao answered the extraordinary erudite policy examination, pointing to the inner court eunuchs as the root of turmoil and disorder; Su with Feng Su and Pang Yan were examiners—fearing and evading, they did not dare report it, and in the end met with the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zao's extraordinary policy examination answer indicted the inner-court eunuchs as the root of chaos; Jia Su, Feng Su, and Pang Yan served as examiners, shrank from reporting it, and ultimately shared the disaster.

sentences.zh: 餗本中立，不肯身犯顏排奸幸以及誅，與王涯實不知謀，人冤之。

translations.literal: Su was by nature neutral; he would not personally risk remonstrance face to face to purge wicked favorites and thus meet execution—he and Wang Ya truly did not know the plot; people considered it an injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Su had always kept to the middle path and would not risk his life remonstrating against corrupt favorites; he and Wang Ya truly knew nothing of the conspiracy, and the public regarded their deaths as a grievous wrong.

sentences.zh: 舒元輿，婺州東陽人。

translations.literal: Shu Yuanyu was a man of Dongyang in Wuzhou commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanyu came from Dongyang in Wuzhou commandery.

sentences.zh: 地寒，不與士齒。

translations.literal: His family was humble; he did not rank with gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and obscure, and he did not stand among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 始學，即警悟。

translations.literal: When he first studied, he was immediately alert and perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: From the moment he took up learning he showed unusual quickness of mind.

sentences.zh: 去客江夏，節度使郗士美異其秀特，數延譽。

translations.literal: He left and sojourned in Jiangxia; Military Commissioner Xi Shimei marveled at his outstanding excellence and repeatedly extended praise.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled to Jiangxia, where Military Commissioner Xi Shimei was struck by his brilliance and repeatedly commended him.

sentences.zh: 元和中，舉進士，見有司鉤校苛切，既試尚書，雖水炭脂炬餐具，皆人自將，吏一倡名乃得入，列棘圍，席坐廡下，因上書言：「古貢士未有輕於此者，且宰相公卿繇此出，夫宰相公卿非賢不在選，而有司以隸人待之，誠非所以下賢意。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi; seeing the examining officials' verification harsh and severe, when he tested at the Ministry of Personnel—even water, fuel, tallow candles, and eating utensils, each person had to carry himself; the clerk had to call one's name before one could enter; they lined thorn fences, sat in ranks under the corridor—thereupon he submitted a memorial saying: "In antiquity presenting tribute scholars was never lighter than this; moreover chief ministers and dukes come forth from this—chief ministers and dukes, if not worthy, are not in the selection, yet the examining officials treat them like bondsmen— truly this is not the way to defer to worthy men below.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination. He found the examiners' scrutiny pitiless: at the Ministry of Personnel test even water, firewood, candles, and tableware had to be carried in by hand; a clerk called each name before entry; candidates sat beneath the eaves within thorn fences. He memorialized: "Never in antiquity were tribute scholars treated so lightly—and since prime ministers and high nobles rise from this gate, only the worthy belong in the selection. Yet officials treat them like servants. That is no way to honor talent.

sentences.zh: 羅棘遮截疑其奸，又非所以求忠直也。

translations.literal: Thorn fences to block and intercept suspect them of treachery—again this is not the way to seek loyal straightness.
translations.idiomatic: Ringing candidates with thorn hedges as though they were criminals is no way to seek loyal and upright men.

sentences.zh: 詩賦微藝，斷離經傳，非所以觀人文化成也。

translations.literal: Poetry and rhapsody are minor arts, severing and splitting the classics— not the way to observe men's culture and completion.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry and fu are minor accomplishments that cut the classics apart—they do not reveal a man's cultivation.

sentences.zh: 臣恐賢者遠辱自引去，而不肖者為陛下用也。

translations.literal: Your servant fears worthy men will withdraw in distant shame and remove themselves, while unworthy men will be used by Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the worthy will withdraw in humiliation while the unworthy are the ones Your Majesty ends up employing.

sentences.zh: 今貢珠貝金玉，有司承以棐笥皮幣。

translations.literal: Now when presenting pearls, shells, gold, and jade, the examining officials receive them on offering trays with leather covers.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute pearls, jade, and gold are presented, officials receive them on lacquered trays wrapped in leather.

sentences.zh: 何輕賢者，重金玉邪？」

translations.literal: Why treat worthy men lightly yet weigh gold and jade heavily?"
translations.idiomatic: Why treat scholars so cheaply and treasure gold and jade so dearly?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「取士不宜限數，今有司多者三十，少止二十，假令歲有百元凱，而曰吾格取二十，謂求賢可乎？

translations.literal: He also said: "Selecting scholars ought not to be limited by number; now the examining officials take at most thirty, at least only twenty—suppose in a year there were a hundred top graduates, yet one says 'I take twenty by regulation'—can that be called seeking the worthy?
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Recruitment should not be capped by quota. Examiners now take thirty at most, twenty at least. Suppose a year produced a hundred top candidates and an official said, 'I take twenty by rule'—would that be seeking talent?

sentences.zh: 歲有才德才數人，而曰必取二十，謬進者乃過半，謂合令格可乎？」

translations.literal: In a year there are only a few men of talent and virtue, yet one says one must take twenty— wrongly advanced men then exceed half; can that accord with regulations and precedent?"
translations.idiomatic: In a given year only a handful may truly have talent, yet twenty must be chosen—so more than half are promoted by mistake. Can that satisfy law and precedent?"

sentences.zh: 俄擢高第，調鄠尉，有能名。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted with highest rank and was transferred as aide of E county; he had a reputation for competence.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he passed with highest honors and was appointed aide of E county, earning a name for ability.

sentences.zh: 裴度表掌興元書記，文檄豪健，一時推許。

translations.literal: Pei Du memorialized [to appoint] him to manage secretarial duties at Xingyuan; his documents and proclamations were bold and strong— for a time he was praised and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du recommended him as secretary at Xingyuan; his dispatches were vigorous and forceful, and for a time he was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，劾按深害無所縱。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor; in impeachment and investigation he was deep and harmful, letting nothing slip.
translations.idiomatic: He was made investigating censor and prosecuted cases relentlessly, sparing no one.

sentences.zh: 再遷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to aide in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to aide in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 元輿自負才有過人者，銳進取。

translations.literal: Yuanyu considered himself talented beyond others and pressed forward aggressively for advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Yuanyu believed his talent surpassed others and pushed hard for promotion.

sentences.zh: 太和五年，獻文闕下，不得報。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taihe, he presented writings at the palace gate and received no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taihe he submitted writings at the palace and received no answer.

sentences.zh: 上書自言：「馬周、張嘉貞代人作奏，起逆旅，卒為名臣。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial stating himself: "Ma Zhou and Zhang Jiazhen had others write memorials for them, rose from roadside inns, and in the end became famous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on his own behalf: "Ma Zhou and Zhang Jiazhen began with memorials drafted for them in humble inns and ended as celebrated statesmen.

sentences.zh: 今臣備位於朝，自陳文章，凡五晦朔不一報，竊自謂才不後周、嘉貞，而無因入，又不露所缊，是終無振發時也。

translations.literal: Now your servant holds a post at court; having presented my own writings, for five new moons there has been no reply. I privately consider my talent not inferior to Zhou or Jiazhen, yet I have no means of entry, nor do I reveal what I hold wrapped in cloth—thus there will never be a time when I can rise and flourish.
translations.idiomatic: I now hold office at court. I have offered my writings myself, yet for five months I have received no answer. I do not think my talent falls short of Ma Zhou or Zhang Jiazhen, but I have no way in, and I will not display the talent I keep bundled away—so I shall never have my moment to rise.

sentences.zh: 漢主父偃、徐樂、嚴安以布衣上書，朝奏暮召，而臣所上八萬言，其文鍛煉精粹，出入今古數千百年，披剔剖抉，有可以輔教化者未始遺，拔犀之角，擢象之齒，豈主父等可比哉？

translations.literal: In Han, Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, and Yan An submitted memorials as commoners—in the morning they memorialized, in the evening they were summoned—whereas the eighty thousand characters I submitted, the text forged and refined to essence, ranging through several thousand years past and present, picking apart and dissecting, never omitting anything that could aid instruction and transformation, plucking the rhinoceros horn, drawing out the elephant tusk—how can they be compared with Zhufu and the rest?
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Zhufu Yan, Xu Le, and Yan An wrote as plain commoners: memorials submitted at dawn brought summons by dusk. My own memorial runs to eighty thousand characters, hammered fine and distilled, ranging across millennia, sifting and parsing what might aid moral instruction—prizing the rhinoceros horn, the elephant tusk. How are men like Zhufu Yan my equals?

sentences.zh: 盛時難逢，竊自愛惜。」

translations.literal: A flourishing age is hard to encounter; I privately cherish myself."
translations.idiomatic: A golden age is rarely met; I must cherish this chance while I can."

sentences.zh: 文宗得書，高其自激卬，出示宰相，李宗閔以浮躁誕肆不可用，改著作郎，分司東都。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong received the letter, he admired his self-exhortation, showed it to the chief ministers, and Li Zongmin, deeming him restless, reckless, and unusable, changed his appointment to Drafting Gentleman and assigned him to the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenzong read the memorial he admired its fervor, showed it to his chief ministers, and Li Zongmin judged him volatile and unfit for office. He was reassigned as Drafting Gentleman and posted to the Eastern Capital branch.

sentences.zh: 時李訓居喪，尤與元輿善。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xun was in mourning and was especially close to Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun was then in mourning and was especially close to Shu Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 及訓用事，再遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: When Xun came to power, [Yuanyu] was promoted again to Left Department Director.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Xun gained influence, Yuanyu was promoted again to Left Department Director.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫李固言表知雜事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Guyan memorialized to appoint [Yuanyu] to manage miscellaneous censorial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Guyan recommended Yuanyu to handle miscellaneous censorial business.

sentences.zh: 固言輔政，權知御史中丞。

translations.literal: Guyan assisted in governing; [Yuanyu] was appointed acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: With Guyan assisting in government, Yuanyu was made acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 會帝錄囚，元輿奏辨明審，不三月即真，兼刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor reviewed prisoners, Yuanyu's memorials of judgment were clear and thorough; within three months he received full appointment and concurrently served as Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During an imperial review of prisoners Yuanyu's rulings were lucid and careful. In less than three months he received full appointment and was also made Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 專附鄭註，註所惡，舉繩逐之。

translations.literal: He attached himself exclusively to Zheng Zhu; whomever Zhu hated, he would raise charges and drive out.
translations.idiomatic: He clung exclusively to Zheng Zhu; anyone Zhu disliked he would impeach and expel.

sentences.zh: 月中，以本官同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Within the month, with his existing office he became Concurrent Grand Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: That same month he was appointed Concurrent Grand Councilor while retaining his existing post.

sentences.zh: 詭謀謬算，日與訓比，敗天下事，二人為之也。

translations.literal: With deceitful plots and mistaken calculations, day by day he matched Xun and ruined the affairs of the realm—the two of them did it.
translations.idiomatic: Scheming foolishly and calculating badly, he daily joined Li Xun in wrecking the empire—those two men did it.

sentences.zh: 然加禮舊臣，外釣人譽。

translations.literal: Yet he added courtesy toward old ministers and outwardly fished for people's praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he showed extra deference to senior ministers and outwardly courted public praise.

sentences.zh: 先時，裴度、令狐楚、鄭覃皆為當路所軋，致閑處。

translations.literal: Earlier, Pei Du, Linghu Chu, and Zheng Tan had all been squeezed by those in power and were relegated to idle posts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Pei Du, Linghu Chu, and Zheng Tan had all been pushed aside by the men in power and left in inactive posts.

sentences.zh: 至是，悉還高秩。

translations.literal: At this time, all were restored to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Now all were restored to high rank.

sentences.zh: 元輿為《牡丹賦》一篇，時稱其工。

translations.literal: Yuanyu composed one piece, "Rhapsody on the Peony," and at the time it was praised as skilled.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyu wrote a "Rhapsody on the Peony," which contemporaries praised as masterly.

sentences.zh: 死後，帝觀牡丹，憑殿闌誦賦，為泣下。

translations.literal: After his death, when the emperor viewed the peonies he leaned on the palace balustrade and recited the rhapsody, weeping.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuanyu's death the emperor, viewing the peonies, leaned on the palace rail and recited the rhapsody until he wept.

sentences.zh: 弟元褒、元肱、元迥，皆第進士。

translations.literal: His younger brothers Yuanbao, Yuangong, and Yuanjiong all passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brothers Yuanbao, Yuangong, and Yuanjiong all passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元褒又擢賢良方正，終司封員外郎。

translations.literal: Yuanbao was also selected through the Exemplary and Upright recruitment and ended as Assistant Director in the Department of Enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanbao was also chosen through the Exemplary and Upright examination and eventually served as Assistant Director in the Department of Enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 余及誅。

translations.literal: The rest were also put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The others were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 王璠，字魯玉。

translations.literal: Wang Fan, courtesy name Luyu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan, courtesy name Luyu.

sentences.zh: 元和初舉進士、宏辭，皆中，遷累監察御史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi and the Hongci examinations, both successfully, and was promoted in succession to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanhe he passed both the jinshi and Hongci examinations and rose through the ranks to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 儀宇峻整，著稱於時。

translations.literal: His bearing was stern and orderly, and he was well spoken of in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing in manner, he enjoyed a strong reputation in his day.

sentences.zh: 以起居舍人副鄭覃宣慰鎮州。

translations.literal: As Attendant Gentleman of the Imperial Diary he served as deputy to Zheng Tan on a pacification mission to Zhen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Attendant Gentleman of the Imperial Diary he accompanied Zheng Tan on a pacification mission to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 長慶末，擢職方郎中，知制誥。

translations.literal: At the end of Changqing he was promoted to Director in the Bureau of Appointments and was put in charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Changqing he became Director in the Bureau of Appointments and was entrusted with drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 時李逢吉秉政，特厚璠，驟拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the time Li Fengji held power and especially favored Fan, who was suddenly appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Li Fengji then held power, favored Fan greatly, and had him abruptly appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 璠挾所恃，頗橫恣，道直左僕射李絳，交騎不避。

translations.literal: Fan, relying on his backing, was quite overbearing; on the road he met Left Vice Director Li Jiang riding abreast, and their mounted escorts did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, emboldened by patronage, grew arrogant. Meeting Left Vice Director Li Jiang on the road, their mounted escorts refused to give way.

sentences.zh: 絳上言：「左右僕射，師長庶官，開元時，名左右丞相，雖去機務，然猶總百司，署位不著姓。

translations.literal: Jiang submitted a memorial: "The Left and Right Vice Directors are elders to the multitude of officials. In the Kaiyuan era they were called Left and Right Chief Ministers; though removed from core affairs, they still oversaw all bureaus, and their posts did not list surnames.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang memorialized: "The Left and Right Vice Directors are superiors to all officials. In Kaiyuan they were called Left and Right Chief Ministers. Though removed from day-to-day power, they still oversaw every bureau, and their seats were not marked with personal names.

sentences.zh: 上日班見百官，而中丞、御史在廷。

translations.literal: On days when the emperor held court and received the hundred officials, the vice censor-in-chief and censors were present in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: On days when the emperor received the hundred officials in audience, the vice censor-in-chief and censors stood in the hall.

sentences.zh: 元和中，伊慎為僕射，太常博士韋謙以慎位緣恩進，削其禮，至僕射就臺見中丞，或立廷中，中丞乃至。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era, when Yi Shen was Vice Director, the Grand Ceremonial Doctor Wei Qian, because Shen's post had been gained through favor, reduced his ceremonial precedence, so that the Vice Director would come to the censorate to see the vice censor-in-chief, or stand in the courtyard until the vice censor-in-chief arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe, when Yi Shen became Vice Director, Grand Ceremonial Doctor Wei Qian—holding that Shen had advanced through favor—stripped his ceremonial rank so that a Vice Director would come to the censorate to wait on the vice censor-in-chief, sometimes standing in the courtyard until the vice censor-in-chief appeared.

sentences.zh: 憲度倒置，不可為法。」

translations.literal: The statutes were inverted and could not serve as precedent."
translations.idiomatic: The hierarchy was turned upside down and could not stand as precedent."

sentences.zh: 逢吉憚絳正，遏其事不奏，但罷璠為工部侍郎，而絳亦用太子少師分司東都，議者不直之。

translations.literal: Fengji feared Jiang's rectitude, blocked the matter from being submitted, but only removed Fan to Vice Minister of Works, while Jiang was also assigned as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent at the Eastern Capital branch office; critics did not consider this just.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji, wary of Jiang's integrity, suppressed the memorial, merely demoting Fan to Vice Minister of Works while Jiang was also sent to the Eastern Capital as Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent. Observers thought neither man had been treated fairly.

sentences.zh: 初，璠按武昭獄，意逢吉德己，及罷中丞，乃失望。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan investigated the Wuzhao case, he thought Fengji owed him a debt; when he was removed as vice censor-in-chief, he was disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan had earlier handled the Wuzhao investigation and assumed Fengji was in his debt; when he lost the vice censorate he felt betrayed.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為河南尹。

translations.literal: After a long while he was sent out as Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was posted out as Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 時內廄小兒頗擾民，璠殺其尤暴者，遠近畏伏。

translations.literal: At the time the stable boys of the inner stud were quite troublesome to the people; Fan killed the most violent among them, and near and far feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Stable boys from the imperial stud were harassing the people; Fan executed the worst offenders, and the region fell quiet in fear.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書右丞，再遷京兆尹。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and was promoted again to Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Right Vice Director of Revenue, then was promoted again to Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 自李諒後，政條隳斁，奸豪浸不戢，璠頗修舉，政有名。

translations.literal: Since Li Liang, administrative rules had collapsed and corrupt strongmen increasingly went unchecked; Fan considerably restored order, and his governance gained a name.
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Liang's time Jingzhao's rules had decayed and local bullies had grown brazen; Fan restored discipline and earned a name for effective government.

sentences.zh: 鄭註奸狀始露，宰相宋申錫、御史中丞宇文鼎密與璠議除之，璠反以告王守澄，而註由是傾心於璠。

translations.literal: When Zheng Zhu's wicked conduct first came to light, Chief Minister Song Shenxi and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding secretly discussed with Fan removing him; Fan instead reported this to Wang Shoucheng, and from this Zhu came to trust Fan wholeheartedly.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Zhu's misconduct first surfaced, Chief Minister Song Shenxi and Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuwen Ding secretly plotted with Fan to remove him. Fan instead informed Wang Shoucheng, and Zhu thereafter placed his trust in Fan.

sentences.zh: 進左丞，判太常卿事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Left Vice Director and concurrently directed affairs of the Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Vice Director and concurrently directed the Ministry of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 出為浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Military Commissioner of Zhexī.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as Military Commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 李訓得幸，璠於逢吉舊故，故薦之，復召為左丞，拜戶部尚書，判度支，封祁縣男。

translations.literal: When Li Xun gained favor, Fan, being an old associate of Fengji, therefore recommended him; [Fan] was recalled again as Left Vice Director, appointed Minister of Revenue, given charge of the treasury, and enfeoffed as Baron of Qi county.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xun rose to favor, Fan—Fengji's old associate—recommended him and was recalled as Left Vice Director, appointed Minister of Revenue with charge of the treasury, and enfeoffed Baron of Qi county.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔得罪，璠亦其黨，見註求解，乃免。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin fell from grace, Fan was also of his faction; seeing Zhu he begged to be released and was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin was ruined Fan, as his ally, appealed to Zhu and was spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 訓將誅宦人，乃授河東節度使，已而敗。

translations.literal: When Xun was about to execute the eunuchs, [Fan] was appointed Military Commissioner of Hedong; soon afterward [the plot] failed.
translations.idiomatic: As Li Xun prepared to kill the eunuchs Fan was made Military Commissioner of Hedong; the plot failed shortly after.

sentences.zh: 璠子遐休，直弘文館，所善學士令狐定及劉軻、劉軿、仲無頗、柳喜集其所，皆被縛。

translations.literal: Fan's son Xiaxiu, on duty at the Hongwen Institute, had gathered there his favored scholars Linghu Ding and Liu Ke, Liu Pi, Zhong Wupian, and Liu Xi—all were bound.
translations.idiomatic: Fan's son Xiaxiu, serving at the Hongwen Institute, had gathered his friends—the academicians Linghu Ding, Liu Ke, Liu Pi, Zhong Wupian, and Liu Xi—and all were seized.

sentences.zh: 定等自解辯，得釋。

translations.literal: Ding and the rest explained themselves and were released.
translations.idiomatic: Ding and the others defended themselves and were released.

sentences.zh: 遐休誅。

translations.literal: Xiaxiu was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaxiu was executed.

sentences.zh: 璠鑿潤州外隍，得石刻曰：「山有石，石有玉，玉有瑕。」

translations.literal: When Fan excavated the outer moat of Run prefecture, he obtained a stone inscription reading: "The mountain has stone; the stone has jade; the jade has a flaw."
translations.idiomatic: While digging Runzhou's outer moat Fan uncovered a stone inscription: "Mountains hold stone; stone holds jade; jade holds a flaw."

sentences.zh: 術家謂璠祖名，生礎，礎生璠，盡遐休，蓋其應雲。

translations.literal: Masters of arts said it matched Fan's ancestral names: Sheng gave Chuo, Chuo gave Fan, exhausting Xiaxiu—this was its fulfillment, they said.
translations.idiomatic: Diviners said the lines tracked Fan's family names—Sheng begot Chuo, Chuo begot Fan, ending with Xiaxiu—and declared the prophecy fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 郭行余者，元和時擢進士。

translations.literal: Guo Xingyu passed the jinshi examination in the Yuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xingyu passed the jinshi examination during Yuanhe.

sentences.zh: 河陽烏重胤表掌書記。

translations.literal: Wu Chongyin of Heyang memorialized to appoint him chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chongyin of Heyang recommended him as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 重胤葬其先，使誌冢，辭不為，重胤怒，即解去。

translations.literal: When Chongyin buried his forebears he had [Xingyu] compose the tomb inscription; [Xingyu] declined and would not do it, and Chongyin in anger immediately dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongyin buried his ancestors he asked Xingyu to write the tomb inscription. Xingyu refused; enraged, Chongyin dismissed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 擢累京兆少尹。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Junior Intendant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Junior Intendant of Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 嘗值尹劉棲楚，不肯避，棲楚捕導從系之。

translations.literal: Once he encountered Intendant Liu Qichu and would not yield; Qichu had his escort seized and bound.
translations.idiomatic: Once he met Intendant Liu Qichu and refused to give way; Qichu had his attendants arrested and bound.

sentences.zh: 自言宰相裴度，頗為諭止。

translations.literal: [Xingyu] stated that Chief Minister Pei Du largely admonished and stopped [Qichu].
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu appealed to Chief Minister Pei Du, who largely intervened to stop Qichu.

sentences.zh: 行余移書曰：「京兆府在漢時有尹，有都尉，有丞，皆詔自除，後循而不改。

translations.literal: Xingyu sent a letter saying: "The Jingzhao prefecture in Han times had an intendant, a commandant, and an aide—all appointed by imperial edict—and later this was followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu wrote: "In Han times Jingzhao had an intendant, a commandant, and an aide, all appointed by imperial edict—a practice later unchanged.

sentences.zh: 開元時，諸王為牧，故尹為長史，司馬即都尉、丞耳。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era, when imperial princes served as prefects, the intendant became chief administrator, and the aide was the commandant and aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaiyuan, when imperial princes served as prefects the intendant became chief administrator while the aide corresponded to commandant and deputy.

sentences.zh: 今尹總牧務，少尹副焉，未聞道路間有下車望塵避者，故事猶在。」

translations.literal: Today the intendant oversees all prefectural duties and the junior intendant assists; one has not heard of anyone on the road dismounting to avoid dust—precedent still stands."
translations.idiomatic: Today the intendant oversees the prefecture and the junior intendant assists; no one has heard of junior officials on the road dismounting to yield in the dust—the old precedent still holds."

sentences.zh: 棲楚不能答。

translations.literal: Qichu could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu had no answer.

sentences.zh: 遷楚、汝二州刺史、大理卿，擢邠寧節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Prefect of Chu and Ru prefectures, Director of Punishments, and promoted to Military Commissioner of Binning.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Chu and Ru, then as Director of Punishments, and was promoted Military Commissioner of Binning.

sentences.zh: 李訓在東都，與行余善，故用之。

translations.literal: Li Xun was in the Eastern Capital and was on good terms with Xingyu; therefore [Xingyu] was used.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun was then in the Eastern Capital and friendly with Xingyu; for that reason Xingyu was brought into the plot.

sentences.zh: 韓約，朗州武陵人，本名重華。

translations.literal: Han Yue was a man of Wuling in Lang prefecture; his original name was Chonghua.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yue, a native of Wuling in Langzhou, had originally been named Chonghua.

sentences.zh: 誌勇決，略涉書，有吏幹。

translations.literal: He was resolute and daring, had read somewhat, and had administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resolute, he had some learning and real talent for administration.

sentences.zh: 歷兩池榷鹽使、虔州刺史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Salt Monopoly Commissioner of the Two Ponds and as Prefect of Qian.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Salt Monopoly Commissioner of the Two Ponds and as Prefect of Qianzhou.

sentences.zh: 交趾叛，領安南都護。

translations.literal: When Jiaozhi rebelled, he took charge as Protector-General of Annan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiaozhi rebelled he was appointed Protector-General of Annan.

sentences.zh: 再遷太府卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted again to Minister of the Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Minister of the Treasury.

sentences.zh: 太和九年，代崔鄯為左金吾衛大將軍，居四日，起事。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Taihe, he replaced Cui Shan as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard; on the fourth day [in office] the plot was launched.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Taihe he replaced Cui Shan as Grand General of the Left Golden Guard; four days later the coup began.

sentences.zh: 約繇錢谷進，更安南富饒地，聚貲尤多。

translations.literal: Yue advanced through revenue and grain posts; having also held the rich lands of Annan, he amassed wealth in especial abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yue had risen through finance and grain offices; his term in wealthy Annan left him with enormous wealth.

sentences.zh: 羅立言者，宣州人。

translations.literal: Luo Liyan was a man of Xuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Liyan was a native of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元末擢進士，魏博田弘正表佐其府。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi; Tian Hongzheng of Weibo memorialized to appoint him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Zhenyuan he passed the jinshi; Tian Hongzheng of Weibo brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 改陽武令，以治劇遷河陰。

translations.literal: He was changed to Magistrate of Yangwu; because of handling difficult affairs he was transferred to Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Yangwu and, for handling difficult cases well, was transferred to Heyin.

sentences.zh: 立言始築城郭，地所當者，皆富豪大賈所占，下令使自築其處，吏籍其闊狹，號於眾曰：「有不如約，為我更完！」

translations.literal: When Liyan first built the walls, the land required was all occupied by wealthy great merchants; he issued orders that they themselves should build at their locations, officials registered the breadth and narrowness, and he proclaimed to the crowd: "If it is not as stipulated, rebuild it for me!"
translations.idiomatic: When Liyan first raised the city walls, every required stretch lay in the hands of rich merchants. He ordered each owner to build the section on his own land, had clerks measure the widths, and announced to the crowd: "Fall short of the mark and rebuild it yourselves!"

sentences.zh: 民憚其嚴，數旬畢。

translations.literal: The people feared his severity, and in several tens of days it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: The people feared his severity and finished within weeks.

sentences.zh: 民無田者，不知有役。

translations.literal: Commoners without fields did not know there was corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants without land never even knew corvée had been imposed.

sentences.zh: 設鎖絕汴流，奸盜屏息。

translations.literal: He set locks to block the Bian River flow, and thieves and smugglers fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: He installed locks to choke the Bian River, and piracy and smuggling ceased.

sentences.zh: 河南尹丁公著上狀，加朝散大夫。

translations.literal: Intendant of Henan Ding Gongzhu submitted a report, and [Liyan] was given the added title Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Intendant Ding Gongzhu memorialized on his behalf and Liyan was granted the added rank Grand Master of Palace Leisure.

sentences.zh: 然倨下傲上，出具弓矢呵道，宴賓客列倡優如大府，人皆惡之，以是稀遷，然自放不衰。

translations.literal: Yet he was arrogant toward subordinates and haughty toward superiors; when going out he displayed bow and arrows and shouted to clear the road; when feasting guests he arrayed singing girls and actors like a great prefecture—all hated him for this, and therefore he was rarely promoted, yet he did not restrain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he looked down on subordinates and defied superiors, paraded with bow and arrows and a cleared road, and entertained guests with singers and actors like a grand prefect—all resented him, so promotions were rare, but he never moderated his ways.

sentences.zh: 改度支河陰留後，坐平糴非實，沒萬九千緡，鹽鐵使惜其幹，止奏削兼侍御史。

translations.literal: He was changed to Treasury Reserve Officer at Heyin; for false leveling purchases he forfeited nineteen thousand strings of cash; the Salt and Iron Commissioner valued his ability and only memorialized to strip his concurrent post as Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He became Treasury Reserve Officer at Heyin; falsifying grain purchases cost him nineteen thousand strings of cash. The Salt and Iron Commissioner, valuing his competence, merely stripped his concurrent censor title.

sentences.zh: 繇廬州刺史召為司農少卿，以財事鄭註，亦與李訓厚善。

translations.literal: From Prefect of Lu he was summoned as Vice Director of the Directorate of Agriculture; through financial affairs he attached to Zheng Zhu and was also thick friends with Li Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from Luzhou as Vice Director of Agriculture, he handled finances for Zheng Zhu and was close to Li Xun as well.

sentences.zh: 訓以京兆多吏卒，擢為少尹，知府事，以就其謀。

translations.literal: Xun, because Jingzhao had many clerks and soldiers, promoted him to Junior Intendant to manage prefectural affairs, so as to carry out their plot.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun, needing Jingzhao's clerks and soldiers, made Liyan Junior Intendant with charge of the prefecture to advance the plot.

sentences.zh: 李孝本，宗室子。

translations.literal: Li Xiaoben was a son of the imperial clan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaoben was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 元和時第進士，累遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi and was promoted in succession to Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe he passed the jinshi and rose to Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 依訓得進，於是御史中丞舒元輿引知雜事。

translations.literal: Relying on Xun he advanced; thereupon Vice Censor-in-Chief Shu Yuanyu brought him in to manage miscellaneous affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through Li Xun's patronage; Vice Censor-in-Chief Shu Yuanyu then put him in charge of miscellaneous censorial business.

sentences.zh: 元輿入相，擢權知中丞事。

translations.literal: When Yuanyu entered the chancellorship, [Xiaoben] was promoted to acting charge of censor-in-chief affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanyu became chief minister, Xiaoben was promoted to acting head of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 顧師邕，字睦之，少連子。

translations.literal: Gu Shiyong, courtesy name Muzhi, was a son of Gu Shaolian.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shiyong, courtesy name Muzhi, was a son of Gu Shaolian.

sentences.zh: 性恬約，喜書，寡遊合。

translations.literal: By nature he was tranquil and restrained, fond of books, and seldom joined company.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet and abstemious by nature, he loved books and kept to himself.

sentences.zh: 第進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 累遷監察御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 李訓薦為水部員外郎、翰林學士。

translations.literal: Li Xun recommended him as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Waterways and as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun recommended him as Assistant Director in the Bureau of Waterways and as Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 訓遣宦官田全操、劉行深、周元稹、薛士幹、似先義逸、劉英誗按邊，既行，命師邕為詔，賜六道殺之，會訓敗，不果。

translations.literal: Xun sent the eunuchs Tian Quancao, Liu Xingshen, Zhou Yuanzhen, Xue Shigan, Sixian Yiyi, and Liu Ying to inspect the borders; once they had departed, he ordered Shiyong to draft an edict granting the six circuits authority to kill them; when Xun failed, it was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun dispatched eunuchs Tian Quancao, Liu Xingshen, Zhou Yuanzhen, Xue Shigan, Sixian Yiyi, and Liu Ying to inspect the frontier. After they left he ordered Shiyong to draft an edict authorizing the six circuits to kill them; the plot failed and the order never went out.

sentences.zh: 師邕流崖州，至藍田，賜死。

translations.literal: Shiyong was banished to Ya prefecture; reaching Lantian, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyong was exiled to Yazhou; at Lantian he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 李貞素，嗣道王實子。

translations.literal: Li Zhensu was a son of Prince Shi of the Dao line.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhensu was a son of Prince Shi of the Dao line.

sentences.zh: 性和裕，衣服喜鮮明。

translations.literal: By nature he was mild and generous; in dress he liked bright colors.
translations.idiomatic: Mild and easygoing by nature, he favored bright clothing.

sentences.zh: 漢陽公主妻以季女。

translations.literal: Princess Hanyang married him to her youngest daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Hanyang gave him her youngest daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 累遷宗正少卿，由將作監改左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court; from Director of Imperial Construction he was changed to General of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Imperial Clan Court, then moved from Director of Imperial Construction to General of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 韓約之詐，貞素知之。

translations.literal: Of Han Yue's deceit, Zhensu knew it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhensu knew of Han Yue's fraud.

sentences.zh: 流儋州，至商山，賜死。

translations.literal: He was banished to Dan prefecture; reaching Shangshan, he was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Danzhou; at Shangshan he was ordered to die.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：李訓浮躁寡謀，鄭註斬斬小人，王涯暗沓，舒元輿險而輕，邀幸天功，寧不殆哉！

translations.literal: The encomium says: Li Xun was restless and scant of strategy; Zheng Zhu a sharp, petty man; Wang Ya dark and muddled; Shu Yuanyu treacherous and light—inviting fortune from Heaven's work, were they not doomed?
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal reads: Li Xun was impulsive and short on strategy; Zheng Zhu a cunning petty man; Wang Ya obtuse and muddled; Shu Yuanyu treacherous and reckless—banking on heaven-sent success, how could they not court disaster?

sentences.zh: 李德裕嘗言天下有常勢，北軍是也。

translations.literal: Li Deyu once said that the realm has a constant pattern, and the Northern Army is it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu once observed that the empire has a fixed order—and the Northern Army is that order.

sentences.zh: 訓因王守澄以進，此時出入北軍，若以上意說諸將，易如靡風，而反以臺、府抱關遊僥抗中人以搏精兵，其死宜哉！

translations.literal: Xun advanced through Wang Shoucheng; at this time he moved in and out of the Northern Army—as if, on the emperor's authority, persuading the generals, it would be easy as bending grass in the wind—yet instead he relied on the censorate and prefectural gatekeepers and wandering clerks to resist the eunuchs and wrest the elite troops; his death was fitting!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun had risen through Wang Shoucheng and already moved freely in the Northern Army; had he spoken as the emperor's voice to the generals, persuasion would have been effortless—yet he chose instead to pit court clerks and gate guards against the eunuchs for control of the crack troops. Small wonder he died as he did.

sentences.zh: 文宗與宰相李石、李固言、鄭覃稱：「訓稟五常性，服人倫之教，不如公等，然天下奇才，公等弗及也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong with Chief Ministers Li Shi, Li Guyán, and Zheng Tan said: "In receiving the Five Constants by nature and submitting to the teaching of human relations, Xun is not your equal; yet as a rare talent under Heaven, you do not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong told chief ministers Li Shi, Li Guyán, and Zheng Tan: "Li Xun may not match you in innate virtue or in the discipline of human relations; yet as a singular talent in the realm, none of you equals him.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「訓曾不得齒徒隸，尚才之雲！」

translations.literal: Deyu said, 'Xun could not even rank with menial attendants—yet you still speak of his talent!'
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu said, 'Li Xun could not even rank with menial attendants—yet you still speak of his talent!'

sentences.zh: 世以德裕言為然。

translations.literal: The age deemed Deyu's words correct.
translations.idiomatic: The age deemed Li Deyu's words correct.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：「國將亡，天與之亂人。」

translations.literal: The Classic of History says, 'When a state is about to perish, Heaven gives it men of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of History says, 'When a state is about to perish, Heaven gives it men of disorder.

sentences.zh: 若訓等持腐株支大廈之顛，天下為寒心豎毛，文宗偃然倚之成功，卒為閹謁所乘，天果厭唐德哉！

translations.literal: If men like Xun propped a rotting stump beneath the pinnacle of a great hall, the realm shuddered and its hair stood on end; Wenzong complacently leaned on them for success, yet in the end was ridden by the eunuch minions—did Heaven truly weary of Tang virtue?
translations.idiomatic: When men like Li Xun propped a rotting stump beneath the pinnacle of a great hall, the realm shuddered and its hair stood on end; Emperor Wenzong complacently leaned on them for success, yet in the end was ridden by the eunuch minions—did Heaven truly weary of Tang virtue?
